articles.title: WSL talking points: London City, Arsenal and Man City make winning starts on opening weekend, but Chelsea and Man Utd stutter
articles.summary: All the key talking points from the opening weekend of the WSL season; London City Lionesses galactico era kicks off with a win, but more consistency is needed to be a threat; Chelsea and Man Utd off the pace and fall behind rivals Arsenal and Man City
articles.body:
Manchester City took some time to find their usual standards but after the nerves were settled by Mary Fowler's opener, they quickly reminded everyone why they are champions and why they will be well amongst the title race once more.

Fowler's chance was gifted to them by Birmingham but the precision made the difference. Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw rising highest on two occasions to glance home her double has already set the tone for another goal-laden campaign.

There is more to come from City, as Jade Rose's error in the 90th minute highlighted, but the fact they can win so emphatically while not at their best will strike fear in the likes of Arsenal and Chelsea as we settle in for another enthralling WSL season.

Arsenal need more but reinforcements helping already

Like Manchester City, Arsenal were short on their usual standards in front of goal. Alessia Russo and Stina Blackstenius both squandered chances from close range but it looks as if Renee Slegers has a few new names to rely on now.

It has been a summer of change at the club but new signings Lisa Baum and Georgia Stanway stood out and were duly needed in the narrow win against Brighton.

Baum introduced herself in perfect fashion with her emphatic opener after dancing into the box. She then stung the hands of Chiamaka Nnadozie with a similar effort after cutting in from the left during the second half.

Despite her age, Baum displays confidence and talent beyond her years and looks ready-made for the WSL.

Meanwhile, Stanway settled into her role as if she had never left the top flight of English football.

The Lionesses midfielder was the first midfielder in history to record 100+ passes on their league debut for a club and dictated play from the middle of the pitch throughout.

There is more to come from Arsenal and they will need their star players to get up to speed quickly if they are to keep pace with City - but for now, it looks like the reinforcements they have added are ready to contribute.

A lot of eyes would’ve been on Chelsea to start the season strongly. For the first time since 2019, they started a WSL campaign not as defending champions. A statement of intent was needed.

The same can also be said of Manchester United. After missing out on the Champions League, the pressure to return was already on. Then came Marc Skinner’s departure and Eva Olid’s appointment. Starting the new era with a win was of utmost importance.

Neither managed to be convincing. For the latter, perhaps some grace can be given. The transition in coaches, the hype surrounding the new-look London City and a transfer window in which Olid admitted the focus had shifted to January meant there was an uphill struggle. The way they were dominated, though, will give the former Hearts boss much to ponder.

As for the Blues, Lauren James’ opener was a positive. Yet, despite 34 total attempts and an xG of 3.6, the majority of Stamford Bridge was left wanting more.

Buurman’s late own goal will be a tough pill to swallow, but is as a result of Sonia Bompastor’s side not putting the game to bed earlier. With Arsenal and Man City getting off the mark with wins, this false start is the last thing the team once at the pinnacle of English women’s football needed. After one game, they are already part of the chasing pack.

Galactico era off and running but London City need consitency

A debut for Alexia Putellas, as well as debuts for Rosa Kafaji, Mapi Leon and Janni Thomsen, grabbed the headlines in the build-up to the game but London City Lionesses didn't need their stars to shine to beat Manchester United.

An own goal from Julia Zigiotti and a moment of magic from Danielle van de Donk were enough to secure the victory. It was comfortable from minute one for the hosts at a sold-out Hayes Lane but consistency will now be at the forefront of everyone's thinking as they push ahead with the season.

It was something that was lacking from their debut campaign in the WSL but now, fuelled by the talent they have recruited in a stunning summer transfer window, it will now be key.

Michele Kang was asked about how the club will measure success this season before kick-off. She was hesitant to say trophies will be needed.

The club have the talent at their disposal to compete for titles this season but consistency is one issue you cannot address in the window. It has to be earned, week in and week out, as a team.

Coming into a new league is always a challenge. Therefore, not getting off to a winning start is not the end of the world. However, the nature of performances is what matters.

In that respect, Birmingham may come away with their heads held high. Being picked to face the champions away from home on the opening day is arguably the worst start imaginable. But for 45 minutes they held their own until finally City’s quality shone through.

Amy Merricks couldn’t have asked for much more. There will be a sense inside the Blues dressing room that if they can replicate that effort and frustrate teams to that extent every game, they will find a way to survive.

For Charlton, though, there will be a sense of disappointment. While Liverpool aren’t a side to be sniffed at, it did take them 13 games last season to get a win. At home, the Addicks may have had higher hopes. But they just weren’t at the races. Vivien Endemann’s quality was a small taste of what they can expect moving forward. If their response continues to be the same, they will surely be in trouble come the end of the season.

Then there’s Crystal Palace, who bounced back in style. A debut goal for Lexi Lloyd-Smith, a clean sheet and a job well done against Everton.

After a year away from the top flight, that was exactly what the doctor ordered. And, to cap it off, it was a good performance. They were close to a second and despite having less of the ball were competitive with Everton, who only truly pushed right at the very end.

articles.title: Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka show Arsenal can level up their attack even without the blockbuster signing they craved
articles.summary: Arsenal missed out on Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez during the summer transfer window but Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka are fit and firing again; champions beat Chelsea 2-1 to claim third straight Premier League win
articles.body:
The Chelsea goalkeeper managed to push his effort around the post. But the slick passage of play was one of many examples of how the champions, on maximum points after a third straight win, are feeling the benefits of having the trio available again.

Much of the focus ahead of the game had fallen on Chelsea's front three. How would Arsenal contain Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer? It seemed the script had been written when Rogers stunned the ground into silence after 77 seconds.

But Arsenal regained their poise and proved a point about their own attack. Rogers was one of three high-profile forwards to elude them during the summer along with Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez. But they may still have the tools to level up without them.

Latest news and rumours: Chelsea | Arsenal

The key is simply to get their best attackers on the pitch, something injuries prevented for much of the last two seasons. This was the first time since December 2024 that Odegaard, Havertz and Saka have started a third straight league game together.

Odegaard and Havertz made the decisive contributions, combining for the winner when the former finished coolly following the latter's dummy. Earlier, Havertz had equalised with his precise finish at Martinez's near post from the edge of the box.

"They have been Arsenal's two best players," said Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville when they were substituted to loud applause. Saka wasn't bad either, tearing into Chelsea on the right and earning a standing ovation of his own later in the second half.

The clamour for Arsenal to add a forward was of course understandable. The club's efforts, although ultimately fruitless, showed they appreciate the need for it. In an ideal world they would have marquee attacking signing leading them into this season.

But they can go at least some way to making up the shortfall by keeping Odegaard, Havertz and Saka fit. The last time they managed it over the course of a full season, in 2023/24, they finished the campaign with a club-record 91 Premier League goals.

It helps that Odegaard has rediscovered his scoring touch.

Their captain is unrecognisable from the player who only scored once in 36 games last term. His winner puts him on three in four for the new campaign; his latest another example, following a nearly-identical goal in the Community Shield, of how he is getting into the box more. Arteta noted other differences.

"He's fit, and confidence-wise I think it's one of the highest that I've seen him," he said. "He also has a point to prove from last season after missing so much football, and Bukayo the same. We missed so many attacking players last season for long, long periods."

His chemistry with both Saka and Havertz is another factor. They were the two players he passed to most against Chelsea. Odegaard found Saka 10 times and Havertz seven. But his understanding with both, the latter in particular, extends to off-the-ball runs too.

"He's a really smart player and moves so well," Odegaard told Sky Sports of Havertz. "He takes defenders' attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind, I'm always free."

Arteta agreed. "When you start to feel the chemistry they have between them and what they can produce, it's great," he added. "For me, he gets to that point because he's enjoying his football.

"And when you are there, you have to enjoy what you do, you have to play with real intent, and that's what I loved to see from him today. He was running forward, he took shots, he created so many situations for his team-mates, so it was great."

Havertz, also on three goals in four games, has been similarly impactful. This was another all-round performance to underline just how much he gives the side, as an aerial outlet and runner in behind who links with his midfielders and works incessantly.

"To displace Havertz from this team, you need to be one of the best players in the world," said Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher.

Three Premier League games in, Odegaard, Havertz and Saka account for all six of Arsenal's goals. But the performance against Chelsea showed it has been a collective endeavour too.

As against Coventry and Aston Villa, Arsenal appeared notably more fluid in the final third, with Havertz often pulling to the right, Saka popping up centrally or even swapping flanks with Christos Tzolis, and Riccardo Calafiori appearing everywhere.

"It was another layer," added Arteta to Sky Sports . "Another layer of dynamism, of threat, of intent, of aggression in the attacking phase. You have certainly seen that today."

Chelsea struggled to cope with the level of movement. Even before the second goal, Arsenal had got in behind their backline repeatedly, their combinations, usually in the right half-space, where Odegaard and Saka, in particular, do their best work, proving problematic.

The challenge now is to keep them fit. A spate of injuries like those suffered in the last two seasons might leave fans pining for that blockbuster signing again. But for now they can enjoy what they have. Odegaard, Havertz and Saka are leading their charge.

articles.title: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea: Gary Neville questions Chelsea's 'all over the place' back three after defeat - but is confident they can finish top three
articles.summary: Chelsea suffered their first defeat under new manager Xabi Alonso, losing 2-1 to Arsenal; Gary Neville was critical of Chelsea's back three - but believes the Blues can finish second or third; Neville: "I'm as positive as I have been for three four five years about Chelsea."
articles.body:
Alonso suffered his first defeat as Chelsea manager at the hands of Premier League champions Arsenal, despite scoring first after just 77 seconds through Morgan Rogers.

Chelsea have now conceded seven goals in three Premier League games - and Neville says the Blues may need to sign more players in their defensive line in order to reach a new level.

He told the Gary Neville Podcast : "The back three, when I watch them, it's almost like their legs aren't connected to their hips and the hips aren't connected to their bodies. It's almost like they're a bit all over the place.

"I look at the sort of best back three probably that I ever saw which was the Juventus and Italy back three with Andrea Barzagli, Leonardo Bonnuci and Giorgio Chiellini - three real giants.

"They worked together as a three, they knew how to position themselves, they were great in the air, they knew how to push up and when to drop deeper. They organised the people in front of them.

"Maybe Chelsea will need to actually recruit more players as they move on through the next year or two with Xabi Alonso. He's done a lot already. He's just needs to get a back three that feels solid. They don't look solid, they look like they're a little bit all over the place. So that that's the main thing right now."

Neville did praise the rest of the Chelsea team though - including wing-backs Pedro Neto and Jorrel Hato, and says they have a great midfield and forward line if they can keep their key players fit.

As a result, Neville believes Chelsea will at least finish third - and could strive for second place on the basis of their start under Alonso.

"I think they can finish second - third is the absolute lowest I can see Chelsea finishing," said Neville. "So that's really good. If you said that to me a year ago, I couldn't see where this project was going.

"I'm as positive as I have been for three four five years about Chelsea because I think they're going in the right direction. It's not perfect, they were always going to be [against Arsenal]. I wouldn't have expected them to win - but that was as good as I felt they could have done in the game.

"They can go home tonight thinking: 'yeah we can take that confidence out of that defeat'. That doesn't sound right does it, when you're at sort of the elite level?

"But I think that those Chelsea fans over there in the corner of the ground that have travelled from Stamford Bridge will be thinking: 'yeah I can buy into what I'm seeing. I like this.'"

Alonso admitted Chelsea need to find solutions to their defensive problems but stressed that it will take time to develop their solidity having only taken the job in May.

"My priority is to win games. Normally you win games when you don't concede many goals.

"It's something we need to address. We need to be tighter, more clinical, more balanced. But this takes time.

"We wanted to compete, win here. We knew we were not that far but it went their way. We could have scored for 2-1 and you never know what happens.

"The result is the result; I can't argue against that. But we need to take it, not happy. It hurts. Disappointed for sure. This is our first defeat.

"I want to compete in the best possible way to win. Today we didn't want to sit deep from the first minute. We want to be active, protagonists in the pressing. We have done many right things. We need to make it better, learn from them.

"When you play at the top level, we want to be as efficient in all the phases of the game. But this is where we are.

"It's game three or four for us in a new phase starting with Chelsea. I'm pleased with the spirit and attitude of the players. They worked hard."

articles.title: Cancer survivors living with chemo hair loss celebrate resilience
articles.summary: The beauty and resilience of women living with cancer is celebrated though photography.
articles.body:
When Rhiannon Thomas lost her hair during chemotherapy just weeks after having a mastectomy, her confidence was at an all time low.

But being photographed for a campaign that celebrates the resilience of women living with breast cancer helped her find an inner strength she never knew she had.

"For the first time I feel I look pretty, I look confident and strong," said the 36-year-old mum.

"It's surprising the strength you find when you go through such a hard time."

Rhiannon, a mother to two daughters aged 14 and nine, was diagnosed with breast cancer after finding a lump while in the shower in November 2025.

"I had an absolute breakdown," said the teaching assistant.

"Like, how do you tell your children? I was so scared to just tell them."

Since then she's had a mastectomy, chemotherapy and is currently having radiotherapy.

When her hair began falling out during chemotherapy she decided to shave her head, but wanted to make it as positive an experience as possible for her children.

She encouraged her youngest to play at being a hairdresser and do whatever she wanted with a scissors before getting the shaver out.

"I was like, 'just cut whatever you want because it's going anyway'," said Rhiannon.

"I wanted to make something hard joyful for my children and for myself because I didn't want them to see me upset, and my daughter loved it."

Footage captured on her phone shows the family laughing at home in Abertridwr, near Caerphilly, as her daughter got creative with the scissors.

But afterwards, in private moments, the radical change to her appearance was hard.

"I remember looking in the mirror and like just crying because it's just you know we don't recognise yourself," she said.

Rhiannon was brought to tears recalling the look on her parents' faces when they first saw her after her head had been shaved.

She took to wearing a head wrap whenever she left the house.

All this sounds very familiar to mental health nurse and mother-of-two Sam Gronow-Walters.

The 44-year-old has also lost her hair though breast cancer treatment.

She was first diagnosed with triple negative breast cancer five years ago, which was successfully treated with intravenous chemotherapy, a lumpectomy and radiotherapy, followed by oral chemotherapy.

But seven months later she found another lump and tests showed it had returned.

A mastectomy followed and she was told she was cancer-free.

In 2024, she was told it had spread to her lung. Last July, tests showed it had spread to her liver and lymph nodes.

"You've got to keep going," said Sam from St Athan in the Vale of Glamorgan.

"You've just got to do whatever you can because I want to see my kids grow up."

Like Rhiannon, when she felt she had no option other than to shave her head, Sam's thoughts were immediately how to make it easier on her children, a daughter aged 20 and a son aged 13.

Her son requested she have her head shaved with a bit left at the front in homage to Brazilian footballer Ronaldo's memorable hairdo at the 2002 World Cup - and she obliged.

"To me that that's quite a happy memory, so he'll see that even when I'm poorly I can still have fun, can still smile and I can still make my children happy and laugh," she said.

Again, she was concerned about the impact her new appearance would have on her children.

"I used to ask my son when I took him to school, 'do you mind if I don't wear a hat?'" recalled Sam.

Rhiannon and Sam first met after signing up to be part of breast cancer charity Pink Ribbon Foundation's BOLD Wales campaign.

The project celebrates the courage and confidence of women who have lost their hair through breast cancer.

Alongside nine other Welsh women they spent a day in Cardiff being photographed by Dutch photographer Caroline Sikkenk.

The photos will be displayed at London's Piccadilly Lights next month.

Both women had been nervous about being photographed but said the experience couldn't have been more joyful.

"It was like we'd all known each other before meeting that day, and we still keep in touch now," said Sam.

Rhiannon had never spoken to another woman who had lost her hair during cancer treatment.

"I just felt really safe and not judged," she said.

Seeing the photos for the first time was emotional for both.

"I was like, 'oh wow'," said Rhiannon, who was proud of the courage it had taken to be photographed at such a vulnerable time.

"I was like, 'wow, that's not me'," she said.

"I was quite proud to show them to my family to say, 'oh, this is me'."

BOLD began in 2022, when Lisa Allen from The Pink Ribbon Foundation met photographer Caroline Sikkenk at a breast cancer conference.

Caroline had spent years photographing women who had experienced hair loss through illness.

"What struck us about her photographs was that these women weren't being shown as patients," said Lisa. "They were strong, beautiful and completely themselves."

The first BOLD shoot took place in 2023.

"What we hadn't anticipated was that we would create a community," said Lisa.

She said the impact often began before a photograph has been taken.

"We set up a WhatsApp group beforehand, so by the time the women arrive they already feel they're going through it together.

"The friendships and support that grow around it last long after the photograph is taken."

Both women said taking part in the project had given them a new-found strength and sense of optimism.

"I feel like my confidence and my positivity just got stronger from the photoshoot," said Rhiannon.

"I walked out of there just so confident and I felt so free and like I don't have to hide."

Gone are the head wraps and proudly showing her shaved head has become "the new normal".

For Sam, the photoshoot helped her find self-acceptance.

"This is me now - I wouldn't have long hair again," she said.

"Hair loss doesn't define who I am. It's just a symbol that I'm getting through this and I am strong."

articles.title: El "mayor error de toda la historia del mercado de fichajes" se deja querer por Mourinho y el Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Scott McTominay, que llegó a ser candidato al Balón de Oro, reconoce que si su 'descubridor' Mourinho le llamase para fichar por el Real Madrid se lo pensaría
articles.summary: Scott McTominay, que llegó a ser candidato al Balón de Oro, reconoce que si su 'descubridor' Mourinho le llamase para fichar por el Real Madrid se lo pensaría
articles.body: Scott McTominay, centrocampista escocés que está triunfando en el Nápoles (ha sido MVP de la Serie A y nominado al Balón de Oro), muestra su admiración por Mourinho y habla de sus problemas de salud en una entrevista concedida al 'Corriere della Sera'. El ex del Manchester United, por el que el Nápoles en 2024 pagó 30,5 millones, sufre de una arritmia cardíaca leve y benigna, por lo que debe someterse a una intervención quirúrgica correctiva en Londres. "Estoy apartado por una arritmia, pero no me preocupa. Me someteré al procedimiento y volveré más fuerte. El Inter no es mejor que el Nápoles", le aseguró el internacional escocés a Monica Scozzafava. En su entrevista compartió que "me siento un líder; no como pizza, pero amo el mar. ¿Redes sociales? La gente inteligente no las necesita". Scott McTominay (29 años) contestó abiertamente a la pregunta de "si te llamara Mourinho para fichar por el Real Madrid, ¿irías?". "Si eso ocurriera, me lo pensaría", reconoció el escocés, que debutó con 18 años en la Premier de la mano de Mourinho. Mourinho, que apostó por McTominay en su época en Mánchester, reconoce que "nadie en el United creía que Scott podría llegar a ser el jugador que es". Mou hizo debutar a McTominay en el primer equipo del Manchester United en mayo de 2017. Durante la temporada siguiente se convirtió en un fijo de sus alineaciones, llegando a sentar en el banquillo a estrellas consagradas como Paul Pogba para darle minutos al joven escocés. En 2018, al ver que McTominay no había sido galardonado en los premios internos de la academia del club, Mourinho creó de forma unilateral el premio 'Manager's Player of the Year' (Jugador del Año para el Entrenador) exclusivamente para reconocérselo al escocés, elogiando su humildad y entrega. Mourinho sigue llamando "my boy" (mi chico) a Scott McTominay, que suma dos títulos con el Nápoles (Serie A y Supercoppa Italiana). La temporada 2024-2025 el escocés firmó 13 goles y 3 asistencias en 35 partidos y el curso 2025-2026 se fue hasta los 14 goles y 3 asistencias en 45 partidos. El histórico Marco Materazzi no dudó en señalar al que él considera como "el mayor error de toda la historia en el mercado de fichajes". Scott McTominay (Nápoles) es un jugador increíble de principio a fin. No entiendo cómo el Manchester United lo vendió por casi nada, porque su valor, en mi opinión, es de 60 a 70 millones de euros o más. Es el mayor error del mercado de fichajes en toda la historia", declaró el exfutbolista italiano en 'Hajper'. Diego Armando Maradona Jr., el hijo del mítico Maradona, declaró que "Después de mi padre, McTominay es el jugador más decisivo en la historia del Nápoles... Es un jugador fundamental". "En el Nápoles teníamos a Dios en la figura de Maradona, pero para mí McTominay es Jesús", dijo el hijo del 'Pelusa' sobre el escocés. Scott McTominay estuvo "en riesgo y bajo observación por su dieta" por culpa de "las lujurias de la cocina napolitana". El centrocampista internacional con Escocia tenía que llevarse cada día a su casa, después de cada entrenamiento, una nota lo que puedo o lo que no puede comer. El periódico 'Il Mattino' advirtió de las "las muchas tentaciones de la cocina napolitana" como el helado, la pizza, la pasta y el queso, que estaban alterando la dieta de un McTominay que estuvo 22 años en el United. El futbolista británico fue seriamente advertido de los peligros para su dieta que podrían significar los productos lácteos napolitanos.

articles.title: Cestero y Sergio levantan la mano
articles.standfirst: Los 'niños' se apuntan como opciones de Mourinho para el once ante el Inter por las numerosas bajas en la medular
articles.summary: Los 'niños' se apuntan como opciones de Mourinho para el once ante el Inter por las numerosas bajas en la medular
articles.body: Cestero o Sergio Martínez podrían ser la gran novedad en el once del Real Madrid en el estreno de Champions del próximo martes, ante el Inter en el Bernabéu. Son dos los caminos que conducen a que uno de los castillistas se pueda convertir en el primer 'niño' al que Mourinho pone a jugar de manera oficial en su segunda etapa en el banquillo madridista. El primer motivo, las numerosas bajas que tiene el técnico en el centro del campo para afrontar el duelo europeo y que dejan a Valverde como único centrocampista disponible. Bernardo Silva, Camavinga y Güler son bajas por sanción y Tchoauméni y Thiago Pitarch por lesión. Los dos últimos ya se ejercitan con el grupo pero, salvo sorpresa, sin opciones de ser titulares y con la duda de que puedan estar en el banquillo. Cinco ausencias que dejan un panorama desolador en la medular del centro del campo. La segunda razón, que el propio Mourinho fue testigo de un plan estratégico para proteger a Cestero y Sergio en su partido con el Castilla del sábado. Cestero jugó el primer tiempo y Sergio lo sustituyó para afrontar el segundo tiempo. Poca carga de minutos para tenerlos listos de cara a la decisión que tome Mourinho sobre quién acompañará a Valverde en el centro del campo. Un partido del Castilla en el que ambos canteranos levantaron la mano ante el portugués. Cestero marcó un golazo para adelantar al filial y gobernó el centro del campo con jerarquía. Sergio Martínez debutó a lo grande con una actuación convincente en la que ofreció detalles de su enorme calidad. El plan con ambos es claro en su condición de candidatos a jugar ante el Inter y ahora es Mourinho el que tiene que tomar la decisión: la primera opción, dar la titularidad a Cestero o Sergio Martínez para no tocar mucho el equipo. La segunda, 'inventar' y descolocar a jugadores para sortear el problema y evitar dar a uno de los canteranos la responsabilidad de afrontar un partido tan comprometido. Si Mourinho se decanta por apostar uno de los dos chavales, la balanza podría decantarse a favor de Cestero. El centrocampista ha hecho toda la pretemporada con el primer equipo, está muchísimo más metido en la dinámica del Real Madrid y desde la pasada temporada ha experimentado lo que es jugar con el primer equipo, con hasta cinco apariciones, una de ellas como titular, en tres competiciones distintas: Liga, Champions y Copa. Fue el gran jefe del centro del campo en el Castilla tanto con Arbeloa como con Julián López de Lerma y en la propia cantera afrontó compromisos de tanta exigencia como la promoción de ascenso a Segunda división o la Final Four de la Youth League conquistada por el Real Madrid. No en vano es el canterano más valioso de La Fábrica, con un valor de mercado de siete millones de euros según la web especializada Transfermarkt. Además, hasta Lisboa tuvo que llegar la frase con la que Arbeloa puso en el escaparate futbolístico a Cestero siendo todavía técnico del Castilla. "Es el Castilla de Manuel Ángel y de Palacios. También de Cestero, que para mí es el mejor 6 de España ahora mismo", dijo Arbeloa en octubre del año pasado de un jugador que fue una de las grandes sorpresas en su proyecto al frente del filial, junto a Thiago Pitarch, y que estaba tirando la puerta abajo del primer filial blanco. Por todas estas cosas, Mou no lo ha perdido de vista y lo ha tenido a sus órdenes desde el primer día de pretemporada. Sergio Martínez ha tenido un impacto espectacular y hay muchas expectativas puestas en él. El joven centrocampista ha dejado detalles de su calidad y se ha ganado muy rápido los elogios. "Los 45 minutos que ha jugado muestran el jugador que es, la capacidad que tiene, su potencial y, sobre todo, la personalidad. Hacer el partido que ha hecho sin apenas conocer a sus compañeros... Estamos contentos con él y sabemos que nos puede ayudar muchísimo durante el año", destacó el técnico del Castilla el sábado tras el debut de Sergio. El joven talento empezó la temporada jugando con el Racing en Primera y la pasada temporada se rodó en la élite disputando más de 300 minutos en Segunda división. Pero su condición de recién llegado juega en su contra. Lleva una semana de vértigo en Valdebebas y apenas está aterrizando. Demasiado pocos minutos y entrenamientos como para adelantar a Cestero en el caso de que Mourinho se decante por apostar por uno de los dos para acompañar a Valverde en el centro del campo. Aparte de los dos 'niños', Mourinho apenas tiene opciones para rearmar el centro del campo con tantas bajas. La principal y única alternativa sin inventar mucho pasaría por retrasar a Bellingham para formar pareja con Valverde. A partir de ahí, para cubrir la vacante que dejaría el inglés en la mediapunta y también la de Güler en el habitual sistema 4-2-3-1 con el que está jugando, el técnico tiene muchas más opciones para completar el tridente en la mediapunta. Brahim, Diomande y el propio Espí podrían ser los elegidos para sortear el grave problema que dejan las cinco ausencias en el centro del campo. Manejar otras opciones supone cambiar el dibujo, y ahí entra la opción de doblar lateral con Dumfries y Trent por la derecha. El inglés podría ejercer de tercer centrocampista junto a Valverde y Bellingham y terminar de reajustar el equipo con Brahim o con el propio Espí en el ataque, junto a Vinicius y Mbappé. Sería por tanto apostar por un 4-3-3 o un 4-4-2 para que encajen las piezas nuevas. La última opción, pero también la más revolucionaria, sería incorporar al mediocampo a Huijsen, con buen pie y físico. Rüdiger y Konaté serían la pareja de centrales y sólo habría que cubrir la baja de Güler con las opciones ofensivas ya mencionadas.

articles.title: El SOS de Cañizares y una medida radical para salvar al Valencia
articles.standfirst: Cañizares propone un "un vaciado absoluto de Mestalla" para que Lim venda: "Sólo el pueblo puede salvar al Valencia"
articles.summary: "El Valencia está herido, está herido de muerte... Y solamente el pueblo puede salvar al Valencia"
articles.body: Santi Cañizares, jugador del Valencia de 1998 a 2008, pide a la afición del Valencia en el programa 'Tiempo de Juego' de la Cadena COPE que siga ejerciendo más presión social sobre Peter Lim para que ponga en venta el club. El exportero destacó, durante la retransmisión del partido que el Valencia acabó perdiendo 0-5 contra el F.C. Barcelona, que "el problema no es perder tres puntos, el problema es mucho más grave y mucha gente tiene ganas de un levantamiento público". "Un vaciado absoluto de Mestalla y de forma reiterada llamaría mucho la atención y provocaría, al menos, el sonrojo de la dirección... Yo no sé si Peter Lim sabe cómo está el equipo ahora mismo, si está viendo los partidos, si le importa lo más mínimo", le subrayó a Paco González. Santi Cañizares advirtió que la propiedad del Valencia únicamente reaccionará si existe un riesgo real de caer a Segunda División. "El propietario empezará a ponerse un poco las pilas y pensar en el mercado de diciembre cuando vea que el chiringuito se le cae abajo", apostó. En un vídeo compartido por el programa 'Tiempo de Juego' Cañizares analizó con más profundidad la grave crisis de un "Valencia herido de muerte". "El Valencia está herido, está herido de muerte. Antes decían en la tanda de mensajes del descanso que, bueno, para que se vaya Peter Lin tiene que haber alguien que quiera comprar el Valencia. El Valencia es un caramelo de empresa, es un caramelo de empresa. Ahí lo tienes, cuarenta y pico mil tíos, cuarenta y pico mil personas van a Mestalla a pesar de que saben que van a sufrir, van a pasar vergüenza. O sea, tiene una masa social extraordinaria", empezó explicando el de Puertollano. Cañizares destacó que "el problema es que Peter Lim no ha querido atender a aquellos que han querido ir a comprar el club. El último no hace más de un año". "Entonces tenemos un problema y es cómo provocar que Peter Lim ponga este club en venta. El siguiente problema será quién lo compra. Pero cómo provocar que Peter Lim ponga este club en venta y nos quite ya y nos despierte de esta pesadilla. Y solamente se puede hacer de una manera, con presión social. Y ya sé que la sociedad y el aficionado no tiene culpa y que tiene mucho mérito por estar ahí, pero solamente con eso", insistió. El guardameta internacional recuerda que "pudieron haberlo hecho los políticos, habiéndole negado la última recalificación y haberle negado el gran negocio que es el Estadio Nuevo, pero no quisieron. Y solamente el pueblo puede salvar al Valencia, aunque no sería justo, no es justo que se le exija".

articles.title: Ole Miss may have survived against Louisville, but Lane Kiffin and LSU loom large after a Week 1 beatdown
articles.summary: Ole Miss delivered a thrilling win over Louisville that didn't feature much defense — something a certain coach had to be happy to see before LSU's Week 3 sh...
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. — For better or worse, and in Trinidad Chambliss' estimation it's mostly for worse, fourth quarter chaos seems to be Ole Miss' happy place. It's not by choice or design, but it's where he often seems to find himself as the quarterback of a team that has raised its fan base's collective blood pressure to alarming levels, even if his own seems to be steady in place.

"I honestly hate these games," he said late Sunday night. "I don't know why we do this every time."

Chambliss, the coolest of cool customers, had just led a drive to set up kicker Lucas Carneiro for a walk-off, 48-yard field goal as time expired, giving Ole Miss a 41-38 win over Louisville to open the season.

It was, in many ways, a more complicated game than it should have been for Ole Miss but also a familiar one. Last season, as the Rebels marched to the College Football Playoff semifinals in the midst of Lane Kiffin's departure to LSU, having the ball in Chambliss' hands late in one-score games practically became their security blanket.

And now that there's just 13 days before Kiffin comes back to Oxford dressed in purple and gold, hopped up on vengeance and armed with a team that delivered pure devastation to Clemson on a muggy Saturday night in the Bayou, we won't have to wait much longer to find out what was better preparation for a blood feud more than nine months in the making.

LSU looked terrifying. Ole Miss looked battle-tested under pressure. And with each passing hour, the first installment of college football's nastiest, most personal rivalry draws ever closer.

"I watched probably two quarters," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said when asked if he had kept an eye on LSU's 51-10 humiliation of Clemson. "I thought they played really good on defense. They've got some really good players up front. I think they are what everybody thought they were going to be on paper."

Unlike Nick Saban, whom he worked under for five seasons, Golding is not the type to avoid the Landshark in the room. What's going to happen two Saturdays from now is monumental — for Kiffin, for the school he left behind, for the SEC and for the never-ending soap opera of college football where what happens on the field is only a fraction of the intrigue.

It's the game that looms over Ole Miss' entire season. Thanks to Kiffin's eternal quest to dominate the zeitgeist and his unquenchable thirst to burn the program he left behind to the ground, it's the night we've been talking about since Kiffin walked out on a playoff team and tried to take everything that wasn't nailed down.

And knowing what we know about human nature, Golding has not had it easy in these past several months. While everyone on the periphery of his ecosystem has been talking about Sept. 19 above all else, he has known that Louisville loomed as a real challenge that could send the Ole Miss season in an entirely different direction if it was not taken care of properly.

"I could be naive, I guess, but I don't think [the noise about LSU] had anything to do with the game," Golding said. "We were not overlooking Louisville at all. It wasn't like there were days [during fall camp] that we were using [to prepare] for other people. We knew we had a lot on our hands. We only get 12 opportunities at this."

Though Golding was granted an extended honeymoon as a new coach — in part because he took over under difficult circumstances and led the Rebels to two playoff wins, in part because he simply isn't Kiffin — there was always going to come a day when those feelings would be replaced by bottom-line comparisons.

And if we are comparing their Week 1 exploits, it's undeniable that LSU looked like a juggernaut and Ole Miss had enough issues that the outcome against Louisville was highly precarious.

You can probably chalk some of that up to typical season-opener sloppiness, along with some new personnel on the back end of the defense that gave up nine plays of 25 or more yards. And you can certainly assign much of the credit to Louisville for being a lively underdog that held up quite well physically in the trenches. Unlike Clemson, which is now an embarrassing shell of the program it used to be, Louisville was a real test that could serve Ole Miss well as it moves forward.

"I like that the bar is where it is right now because that's a real football team and they're going to have a good season," Golding said. "That was a heavyweight fight and we got punched in the mouth a lot and we didn't always respond the right way. It's going to happen in the game. Are you going to pick yourself up or not? And I think we had a lot of guys that did that. But we've got to get a little tougher, and that starts with me."

Logically, Golding is correct. Week 1 in college football is often a liar, and there's tremendous value in beating a team like Louisville on a neutral field as you prepare for an even tougher heavyweight fight in two weeks.

But emotionally, watching Ole Miss play like it did Monday against a team with lesser talent plants that seed of doubt for perhaps the first time since Kiffin left: Is this program really going to keep rolling the way it did?

Golding may turn out to be a fantastic head coach, but his impeccable management of last year's post-Kiffin playoff run is a different challenge than what he faces now that he's fully in charge and reshaping everything in his own image.

And it's not just about losing Kiffin. When you lose a great coach, a brain drain follows out the door. That includes Charlie Weis, Jr., the outstanding offensive coordinator who stayed in place through the playoffs before going to LSU.

Ole Miss may have some of the same stars on the field, like Chambliss, running back Kewan Lacy and receiver Deuce Alexander, but it is a fundamentally different program.

That might be hard for Ole Miss fans to wrap their minds around when Golding's main job last December was to keep everything the same. It might be excruciating if Kiffin builds the kind of championship team at LSU that Week 1 suggests he might have built.

As an institution, Ole Miss has invested a lot in this season. It was a tooth-and-nail fight for Golding to keep Chambliss and others that Kiffin wanted to take with him, and losing to Louisville would have been a disaster — even if playing in this kind of high-stakes, high-intensity game right out of the gate was likely the best thing that could have happened to them.

Golding's job as coach is to take the long view and build a sustainable program. But deep down, he surely understands there is no time to waste.

"There's flashes of an elite football team and there's flashes of a bad football team," Golding said. "There's a lot to learn from this tape. That's our job as coaches."

Job One is done, but the Lane Train is coming — along with the chaos where Ole Miss feels most at home.

articles.title: El Europa denuncia otro 'caso Estelada': "Lo han querido obligar a decir que era español"
articles.standfirst: "Los agentes lo han agarrado por el cuello, lo han lanzado al suelo y lo han golpeado"
articles.summary: "Los agentes lo han agarrado por el cuello, lo han lanzado al suelo y lo han golpeado"
articles.body: El Club Esportiu Europa, equipo del barrio de Gràcia de Barcelona milita en la Primera Federación, denuncia un supuesto caso de represión a un aficionado por mostrar la estelada (bandera no oficial que usan los partidarios de la independencia de Cataluña). El Europa acusa a la Policía Nacional de tener una "desproporcionada actuación" sobre un aficionado de su equipo "por el hecho de mostrar una bandera estelada". "Los agentes lo han agarrado por el cuello, lo han lanzado al suelo y lo han golpeado", denuncia el Europa. En su comunicado el Europa sostiene que, según los testigos, los agentes de la Policía Nacional "le han requisado la estelada e incluso lo han querido obligar a decir que era español, al tiempo que ha sido amenazado con una posible sanción en aplicación de la Ley del Deporte". Los aficionados del Europa "han abandonado la grada visitante en solidaridad con el aficionado". "Desde el Club Esportiu Europa condenamos firmemente la actuación de la Policía Nacional y consideramos inadmisible cualquier actuación que vulnere los derechos fundamentales, la libertad de expresión y las libertades políticas y sociales", compartió el club catalán, que acabó empatando 0-0 en su visita a Alcorcón. El Europa recordó el incidente de un aficionado del F.C. Barcelona con la Policía Nacional en Elche: "Cabe recordar que esta no es la primera vez esta temporada que un aficionado de un equipo catalán recibe una actuación desproporcionada de los cuerpos de seguridad por el hecho de llevar una estelada y consideramos especialmente grave que se vuelvan a producir situaciones de este tipo". Tras el incidente de la Policía Nacional con un seguidor del F.C. Barcelona en Elche el Europa compartió que "manifestamos nuestro rechazo absoluto a cualquier muestra de abuso policial ya la restricción de las libertades individuales. Los estadios no pueden convertirse en espacios de coacción ni vulneración de los derechos fundamentales de la ciudadanía. Y no hablemos de nada lejano. En los últimos años nuestra afición lo ha sufrido en los desplazamientos de nuestros primeros equipos masculino y femenino en Huesca, Madrid o Murcia, por poner tres ejemplos". "Defendemos que la libertad de expresión es un derecho innegociable que debe ejercerse sin ningún miedo ni represalia. Esta defensa no depende de un club ni de un color, sino de un compromiso colectivo que interpela a todo el tejido deportivo. Por todo ello, hacemos un llamamiento a nuestra afición a llenar las gradas de Can Dragó de estelades, convirtiendo nuestro campo en un clamor firme por la dignidad y los derechos civiles", publicó en Instagram. "Paralelamente, alentamos al resto de entidades deportivas del país a sumarse a esta iniciativa ya levantar la voz en sus respectivos estadios. El deporte catalán debe ser un frente común, activo y ejemplar en la protección de las libertades de todos", compartió en su comunicado. "Desde el Club Esportiu Europa queremos denunciar públicamente la lamentable situación que ha sufrido un aficionado de nuestro club durante el partido que estamos disputando contra el Alcorcón. Al inicio del partido y según explican diversos testigos, un aficionado europeísta ha sido objeto de una desproporcionada actuación de unos agentes de la Policía Nacional por el hecho de mostrar una bandera estelada. El aficionado se ha identificado y en todo momento ha seguido las indicaciones que le han dado los agentes. A pesar de ello, según explican otros aficionados que allí presentes, los agentes lo han agarrado por el cuello, lo han lanzado al suelo y lo han golpeado. Además, relatan que le han requisado la estelada e incluso lo han querido obligar a decir que era español, al tiempo que ha sido amenazado con una posible sanción en aplicación de la Ley del Deporte. Cabe recordar que esta no es la primera vez esta temporada que un aficionado de un equipo catalán recibe una actuación desproporcionada de los cuerpos de seguridad por el hecho de llevar una estelada y consideramos especialmente grave que se vuelvan a producir situaciones de este tipo. Ante este lamentable episodio, los aficionados europeístas han abandonado la grada visitante en solidaridad con el aficionado. Desde el Club Esportiu Europa condenamos firmemente la actuación de la Policía Nacional y consideramos inadmisible cualquier actuación que vulnere los derechos fundamentales, la libertad de expresión y las libertades políticas y sociales. El Club Esportiu Europa defiende los derechos y las libertades de todos los aficionados y expresa su plena solidaridad con el joven y con toda la afición europeísta, así como su compromiso de continuar defendiendo los derechos de nuestra gente ante cualquier situación de vulneración o abuso".

articles.title: Valdano retrata la primera derrota del Madrid de Mourinho: "Inoportuna. Interrumpe un Madrid feliz"
articles.standfirst: "Lo entiendo como un partido extraordinario, en el sentido literal de la palabra. Fuera de lo normal, fuera de lo ordinario
articles.summary: "Lo entiendo como un partido extraordinario, en el sentido literal de la palabra. Fuera de lo normal, fuera de lo ordinario
articles.body: Jorge Valdano, jugador del Real Madrid de 1984 a 1987 y entrenador del equipo merengue de 1994 a 1996, analizó 'Movistar Plus Deportes' la primera derrota en partido oficial del Real Madrid en la era Mourinho. "Bueno, inoportuna. Interrumpe un Madrid feliz, que daba la sensación de ir creciendo partido tras partido", dijo Valdano sobre el partido que el Real Madrid de Mourinho acabó perdiendo 1-0 contra el Real Betis. El exfutbolista de 70 años calificó la derrota de "sorprendente" y compartió que "me dio la sensación de que la alineación del partido frente al Betis, es la más cercana a la titular que puede poner el Real Madrid" "Era la primera vez que jugaban todos, que tenía a todos a su disposición, y el resultado fue un golpe duro", subrayó. Jorge Valdano compartió sobre el Real Madrid que "me da la sensación de que se trata de un equipo muy, muy dotado técnicamente, con mucho gol, que fue precisamente lo que le faltó en Sevilla." "Lo entiendo como un partido extraordinario, en el sentido literal de la palabra. Fuera de lo normal, fuera de lo ordinario", dijo sobre la derrota del equipo de Mourinho. Jose Mourinho declaró, después de la derrota contra el Betis en Sevilla, que "no sé por qué hemos perdido, hemos jugado muy bien". "Puedo cambiar de opinión mañana, pero hoy, con las sensaciones del banquillo, no sé por qué hemos perdido porque colectivamente hemos jugado muy bien. No tengo nada que reprochar a ningún jugador por su actitud. Merecemos ganar, pero el merecer no te da puntos", dijo en rueda de prensa.

articles.title: Milo Beimers: How a goalkeeper's van trip ended with a new club
articles.summary: After setting out on a van journey to find a new club, goalkeeper Milo Beimers has signed for Viterbese in Italy in an unexpected turn.
articles.body:
When Milo Beimers set off on a van journey around Europe to find a new club, the final destination was always unknown.

Along with his dad Kevin and their converted transit van, the plan was to travel about 2,000 miles from Belfast to Spain , and eventually into Portugal.

The 18-year-old former Glentoran goalkeeper had a number of trials lined up but no idea where the next step of his footballing career would be.

After 30 days on the road, Beimers has signed for Viterbese, who play in a medieval city an hour outside of Rome in Serie D - the fourth tier in Italy.

"There's been a lot of ups and a lot of downs, but in the end it's worked out and the risk has paid off," said Beimers.

"Living in a van is something new and I'll maybe never do it again, but we've learned a lot from it.

"I'm really proud to find a club and continue my journey in Europe."

Destination unknown - goalkeeper's 2,000-mile van trip to find new club

After he left Glentoran, where he had been from the age of 13, the initial plan for Beimers, his dad and their van was a 2,000-mile journey with a number of trials.

It was far from the traditional route to find a new club, and it is perhaps no surprise it took Beimers to an unexpected place.

He had a trial with Hercules in Spain, and then flew back to London for another opportunity but a call took him to Italy.

After one month on the road, the successful trial led to him signing with Viterbese to achieve his goal of finding a new club.

"When I came back from England, there was a week where nothing was happening and then suddenly I'm getting signed for a club," said Beimers, who is a Canada youth international.

"My mum always says life moves really slow and then it moves really quickly all of a sudden, and that's exactly what's happened.

"There was a moment of realisation whenever I signed that was just like 'I've done it'.

"You have all this stress built up. You have all these questions like 'why is this not working?' But then to suddenly sign is amazing."

Viterbese were relegated to Serie D last season and Beimers says part of the appeal is wanting to get them promoted back to the third tier.

For the new season they have merged with another club under the banner of Vigor Campagnano Gialloblu, but Viterbese is still their home and DNA.

But that was not the only thing that attracted him to the club, with the facilities, a 7,000-seater stadium and people behind the scenes also key.

"They've been through a lot in the history of the club, and the the people are a big thing for me. I care a lot about how it's like off the pitch.

"Sometimes you just have to go with it and go with your gut."

He wants to establish himself as first choice but his main goal is to help the team back to Serie C, which he says would be "amazing".

Beimers made his debut on Sunday and kept a clean sheet in a 4-0 win over Anagni.

Before he set off on his travels, Beimers had spoken of his dreams of facing Barcelona or Real Madrid.

Now, if the luck of the draw falls his way, he could face the likes of Napoli, Roma or either of the Milan giants in the Coppa Italia.

Eventually, he may even work his way through the divisions where big matches become a regular occurrence.

"That would be unbelievable. I don't think I've even processed that yet," he said.

"To draw against someone that big would be unbelievable. It would be one of the biggest matches in my career."

In the spirit of pushing himself out of his comfort zone, Beimers does not speak Italian while most of his team-mates do not speak much English.

He had initially intended to learn Spanish to help him integrate on his journey, but now Italian is at the top of his agenda with his new team-mates helping him out to help him settle in to his new home in Viterbo.

"The people are so welcoming and they are very open to teaching you stuff.

"I'm slowly getting to grips with it and every day I'm getting better."

On the pitch, he adds the coaching techniques are also something new to learn.

"The Italian style is so different, from the techniques, the way I dive or the way I catch corners.

"It's all new to me so it will take a bit of time to learn it, but I'm excited for it and I'm ready to learn.

"Football is its own language. It's not really the words you say, it's more how you say it. Everyone seems to understand it."

Beimers had hoped the adventure would bring him closer to his dad, who is a Canada-born video game designer, and he says he was "the perfect guy to do it with".

"It was a long trip with a lot of ups, downs and silly arguments over nothing.

"But it's been great and it definitely has brought us closer together. He's a huge part of my life and I've got to hang out with him, which has been great."

Beimers documented his journey on social media and as well as showing the ups and fun aspects of their trip, he was also open about the struggles that come from trying to forge a career away from home, such as home sickness and loneliness.

He says it was important for him to show that side of things, and he wanted to be honest about his experience and not just show off the ideal way of living.

"I missed my friends and family, it was difficult to be away from them.

"There was also the uncertainty of not knowing where you're going, not knowing if it's going to work.

"It's important to show that it can be hard, even when it looks great all the time."

And what about the van, the unsung hero of the journey that had become a travelling home on wheels for father and son?

Beimers and his family converted it after his sister, Charlie, purchased it when it was in "bad shape".

After three attempts to get it through its MOT, the van held up throughout the journey and it will remain in Europe for a new adventure - back with its original owner.

"Her original plan to was go all around Europe in it, and we were just borrowing it for the time being.

"My dad is flying back home and I'm staying here, but she deserves to have it back."

After successfully finding a new club through a unique method, Beimers hopes his journey will inspire other young players to try something similar.

"I've hopefully taught some people that if opportunities don't come to you, then you have to create them yourself.

"Hopefully when I talk about, 'oh, it's been lonely here', it tells people that it's not going to be easy.

"But anything you really want in life is not going to be easy, and hopefully it inspires others to do the same."

articles.title: El Valencia se acostumbra a la mediocridad
articles.standfirst: El club se zambulle en una grave crisis deportiva con Corberán como principal señalado; Ron Gourlay, en una realidad paralela; y Kiat Lim, de espectador
articles.summary: El equipo se zambulle en una grave crisis deportiva con Corberán como principal señalado; Ron Gourlay, en una realidad paralela; y Kiat Lim, de espectador
articles.body: El Valencia empezó la temporada perdiendo partidos, sin un plan de juego y sin alma. La goleada ante el Barcelona no solo es un síntoma más de la mediocridad en la que se ha instalado el equipo sino la confirmación de la vulgaridad que guía su proyecto deportivo desde hace varios años. Los cánticos dirigidos a Carlos Corberán, la directiva, Peter Lim y el propio Kiat Lim no son fruto de una tarde de calentón sino la consecuencia de años de desgaste, decepciones y promesas incumplidas. Y por qué no, también una respuesta a la soberbia pública mostrada por el CEO de Fútbol, Ron Gourlay. Pero el gran problema del Valencia actual no es únicamente deportivo, aunque es el más evidente y el más dañino en un club de fútbol. La auténtica crisis es mucho más profunda porque afecta a la relación entre el club y su gente. Hoy existe una fractura social evidente. Mestalla no cree en quienes toman las decisiones. Y cuando un club pierde el apoyo de la afición, entra en una espiral difícil de detener. Kiat Lim eligió uno de los escenarios más arriesgados para estrenarse en el palco de Mestalla en un partido de Liga. Porque el equipo lleva un punto, porque su CEO de Fútbol, había ejecutado una rueda de prensa con un bidón de gasolina para explicar un mercado de verano en el que faltaron al menos dos refuerzos (un delantero y un central). Y, sobre todo, porque estaban anunciadas las movilizaciones. Su actitud es la del espectador que llega a la función en el segundo acto y que se levanta antes de terminar. Cuando ,en realidad, es el productor de la obra. Pero es Carlos Corberán el que acapara todas las críticas. El entrenador ha hecho propias las excusas del club para no reforzar el equipo convenientemente. Y ahí se convierte en el escudo de todos: si el equipo solo ha marcado un gol y ha encajado nueve en cuatro partidos el responsable es él. Y no es que hubiera muchas esperanzas de encontrar en el técnico una voz reivindicativa. Su resignación y alineamiento con el discurso oficial solo podrían sostenerse si hiciera funcionar al equipo. La realidad deportiva es imposible de maquillar. Sobre todo, porque la viene arrastrando desde hace años. El Valencia vuelve a transmitir la sensación de que su única pelea será (es) la supervivencia. Cuatro jornadas y un punto son una carta de presentación alarmante sin contar con la imagen de vulnerabilidad que ofrece el equipo. Ni compite bien ni posee la calidad suficiente para compensar sus limitaciones. El problema no es que se haya instalado en la mediocridad, sino que lleva tanto tiempo que se ha acostumbrado a sobrevivir en ella.

articles.title: Hibernian crisis: David Gray under pressure at Edinburgh club
articles.summary: Hibernian head coach David Gray is under increasing pressure after a drab defeat at St Johnstone on Sunday, but what has gone wrong in recent weeks?
articles.body:
Ten days ago, Hibernian were six minutes away from creating history and reaching the league phase of the Conference League.

David Gray, already lauded in Leith for his Scottish Cup heroics as a player, would have been glorified to an even greater extent.

Never before has a Hibs side reached league phase - or group stage - football in Europe. They could almost touch it, and the riches that come with it.

But then there was a complete capitulation against Gent as they fell at the final hurdle for the second year running.

One week later - after beating Dundee in between - they were back at Easter Road for the first Edinburgh derby of the season. Only a win would suffice, but it was Hearts who emerged victorious.

Victory against St Johnstone on Sunday would not have atoned for a bruising derby defeat, but it would have boosted morale.

Instead, a lifeless and rudderless Hibs side huffed and puffed to a lacklustre loss in Perth, leaving supporters shaking their heads, pointing their fingers and venting their frustrations at Gray and his players.

The head coach cut a dejected figure at full-time and in his post-match interviews after a performance that, once again, left him with a raft of questions about his team and the direction they are headed.

Fowler doubles gives St Johnstone win over struggling Hibs

Deflated and rather despondent, there was a shift in Gray's manner after the action at McDiarmid Park.

How long ago must the post-match celebrations in Gent following their goalless draw in the first-leg feel for him?

He would be forgiven for admitting being confused by his team, because it's certainly how many other onlookers are feeling.

Last weekend at Dens Park, they played some glorious football. They started the second half of the derby well on top, and looked good value for an equaliser before Jack Iredale's mind-boggling red card.

But at times on Sunday, they were like a bunch of strangers searching for someone to step up, take control and grab... something, anything.

Instead, two of Gray's supposed leaders let him down.

Although only signed in the summer, Jason Kerr, the boyhood Hibee - who captained St Johnstone to their 2021 cup double - inexplicably allowed Josh Fowler a simple tap-in from close range before skipper Martin Boyle - who was hooked at half-time - committed a clumsy foul in the box for a clear-cut penalty.

Hibs have now failed to win any of their past 18 league games when conceding first.

"The manner in which we lost the two goals today summed up our first-half performance," Gray told BBC Sport Scotland.

"We were nowhere near aggressive enough to stop the ball coming into the box. We were very passive, gambling and guessing in the box rather than staying goal side.

"Then, we give away a needless penalty which you just can't do.

"You can't give two goals away like that and not come under criticism for it and I know that's my responsibility."

'I don't know what Hibs are trying to do'

While he is taking responsibility, it doesn't look like his players are on the pitch.

Jamie McGrath could leave McDiarmid Park with considerable pass marks, but he was the exception.

Of course, Gray has to shoulder some of that. It's his plan - or otherwise - they are attempting to carry out, but they looked devoid of direction on the field.

"When I watch Hibs, I don't know how they're trying to score goals, I don't know what they're trying to do," former Scotland defender Charlie Mulgrew said on Premier Sports.

"That's the first time I've watched St Johnstone this season and I can clearly see what they're doing.

"Hibs are scratching for something. It's not like they're going, 'this is our style, this is what we're doing and we're just going to hammer home with that - even if we don't do it right'.

"They completely changed the midfield on Thursday, they made two changes at half-time against St Johnstone, I don't see what they're trying to do."

Although towering forward Nathan Lowe netted his first Scottish Premiership goal, the striker has flattered to deceive since joining on loan from Stoke City.

One of Hibs' plays is to punt the ball up to the 20-year-old and although it seldom sticks, Gray is persisting with the striker for now.

Perhaps of greater concern is that his pool of available defenders shrunk further when Grant Hanley gingerly left the field with a hip issue.

Pre-match, the head coach bemoaned his lack of options at the back. Jordan Obita limped off against Hearts with a calf issue and Marko Ivezic was not ready after signing on deadline day as Warren O'Hora's replacement.

O'Hora, 27, was a commanding figure in the Hibs backline and regularly performed admirably with the armband in Joe Newell's absence.

His departure for Leicester, one year after losing star striker Kieron Bowie, was a big blow for Gray and Hibs. Another one.

Gray assured he "still has the group" and believes he will be able "to show the players why I think this can turn very quickly".

Hibs go to Ross County in the League Cup quarter-finals on Saturday before back-to-back home matches against Kilmarnock and Aberdeen.

It feels like nothing short of three wins will be accepted after their latest aimless performance.

Grant: Think the time is sadly up for Gray. Been hoping for things to pick up but that performance today lacked any identity of what the team wanted to do from start to finish.

Ralph: We're such a hard watch at the moment, dreadful on Thursday and dreadful today - there was no reaction from the players whatsoever.

Our style of football is as flat as a pancake - dire, not enjoyable and not entertaining. At this rate I'm strapping in for a painfully long season. Again painful to say but Sir David Gray, 'tick tock'.

Niall: Genuinely what is the point anymore? It's the same season after season at this stage and won't be changing anytime soon, because the club are happy enough for it to be this way. Badly out of his depth, the manager needs sacked, but in fairness who else would take this job on? Shocking, shocking, shocking.

Nick: Just dreadful, a real lack of commitment. Think Sir DG has lost the dressing room - so sad to see but a pure lack of ambition from the players. He will soon become Mr DG at the club.

John: Awful boring football, side to side at the back and slow going forward. Take the shackles off and start playing attacking football. That's me finished until the performances improve. I will get pelters for saying that but it's my opinion.

articles.title: López Catalán, ambicioso en el regreso del Betis a la Champions: "Vamos a disfrutar... y a competir"
articles.standfirst: El vicepresidente del Betis señala que el objetivo en el torneo es "llegar lo más arriba posible"
articles.summary: El vicepresidente del Betis señala que el objetivo en el torneo es "llegar lo más arriba posible"
articles.body: José Miguel López Catalán, vicepresidente del Betis, ha atendido a los medios de comunicación en el Aeropuerto de San Pablo de Sevilla antes de que la expedición verdiblanca, con el primer equipo, acompañado por el juvenil que disputa la Youth League, pusiera rumbo a Francia, donde mañana se enfrenta al Lille en la primera jornada de la Fase de Liga de la UEFA Champions League. Máxima ilusión en la vuelta a la Champions: "La verdad que sí. Aunque no queríamos nunca hablar de Champions por no meternos nosotros esa presión, lo hemos tenido siempre metido en nuestra cabeza y en nuestra ilusión como un sueño. Y ya estamos aquí. Vamos con mucha ilusión y vamos a disfrutarlo". Intentar arrancar con una buena versión: "Sí, por supuesto. Nosotros pensamos que afrontamos esta Champions con una plantilla y con un equipo con todo preparado para hacer un buen papel. Vamos dispuestos a competir y dispuestos a disfrutarlo también". ¿El objetivo es sólo participar? "No, para nada. Tú sabes que somos muy competitivos en este sentido y el objetivo es llegar lo más arriba posible. Aquí lo que funciona es ir partido a partido, y este primero es muy importante. Además, después del sorteo que nos ha tocado, el rival de mañana, el Lille, va a ser un partido importante y cada punto va a contar al final para esa posibilidad de clasificarse para la siguiente ronda". Un partido clave para el objetivo: "Sí, al final sí. Si analizamos el sorteo y esos tres últimos partidos que tenemos con los equipos, se supone, más fuertes (con Arsenal, con Dortmund y con Bayern Múnich), estos cinco primeros partidos son muy importantes y, como siempre, empezar bien el primero es clave". El triunfo ante el Real Madrid y las palabras de Mourinho: "Por supuesto que empezar bien la temporada es muy importante, eso lo sabemos siempre, aunque muchas veces por alguna razón no se consigue. Este año hemos empezado muy bien, con nueve puntos de doce, magnífico. La victoria del viernes fue un paso muy importante a nivel anímico, moral y de alegría para todos, y creo que fue además muy merecida. El equipo lo dio todo, la afición animó como siempre hace y entiendo que Mourinho o los madridistas tuvieran su frustración porque hicieron un buen partido, pero fallaron de cara a puerta y nuestro portero acertó. Estamos muy satisfechos del partido del viernes, pero ya sabemos que eso no vale para nada. Ahora lo importante es el partido de mañana y estar muy concentrados. Esa es la línea: muy concentrados, partido a partido, y mañana es muy importante". La reacción de la afición tras el mercado: "El mercado de fichajes siempre lleva a eso, es un poco un show, con muchas expectativas e ilusión por caras nuevas. Nosotros realmente hemos estado muy tranquilos este verano con una hoja de ruta muy clara. Creemos que hemos hecho una buena planificación y que hemos conseguido cubrir los puestos que queríamos: lateral izquierdo, pivote y delantero centro. Luego hemos acabado además con la guinda de poder traer a Dani Ceballos, que es muy importante para nosotros. Creemos que tenemos una plantilla muy buena, estamos contentos con la planificación y ahora, desde luego, en el campo es donde hay que hablar y donde al final del año se darán las notas". Ceballos, ya en la convocatoria: "Sí, la verdad es que lo esperaba porque él venía con muchísimas ganas. Es verdad que el día del Madrid era imposible porque estaba recién llegado, pero viene con muchísima ilusión. Necesita un rodaje, como es normal, pero ya te digo la ilusión que tiene e incluso, por lo que nos están comentando de estos primeros entrenamientos, la incorporación de Dani al equipo va a ser muy positiva". Pellegrini, ¿satisfecho? "Sí, yo creo que Manuel durante todo este verano ha estado muy contento y satisfecho con el equipo. Luego todos sabemos que todos los entrenadores quieren más y quieren mejorar las plantillas, que siempre son mejorables, pero sinceramente estamos todos muy satisfechos. En el tema del centro del campo creemos que está cubierto: ha salido Amrabat y ha venido Facundo Bernal, que lo está haciendo muy bien y en quien confiamos mucho. Ha salido Altimira y ha venido Dani Ceballos, así que creemos que está todo bastante cubierto. Estamos muy contentos y ahora vamos a por todas". ¿Descartan alguna salida a mercados aún abiertos? "Nunca se descarta porque sabemos que hay algún jugador que cuenta menos y, mientras haya algún mercado abierto, estamos abiertos a ello, pero realmente no hay una actividad importante sobre eso y consideramos que la plantilla está básicamente cerrada". Margen salarial para fichar en enero: "No, no ha quedado remanente. Nosotros, como hacemos siempre, vamos al límite máximo en cuanto al límite de LaLiga y agotamos todo. Aun así, como funciona esto y está muy vivo, cuando sea enero se valorarán los ingresos y los gastos que ha habido por si realmente hay alguna partida más. Pero lo normal, y ojalá sea así porque creemos que lo hemos hecho así muchos años y es correcto, es no hacer nada en enero porque todo vaya bien y en buena línea. Enero debe ser un mercado por si has tenido alguna lesión importante o algo así; ese es el plan". La repetición del penalti del viernes: "Entiendo que fuera muy polémico en ese momento porque es verdad que casi nadie se sabía del todo la norma, pero creo que ha quedado bastante claro que el CTA lo ha aclarado suficientemente y, al final, esa jugada ya no se va a repetir".

articles.title: Rodri se los ha ganado a todos
articles.standfirst: Líder en el campo y también en el vestuario
articles.summary: Líder en el campo y también en el vestuario
articles.body: El Barcelona no tenía la intención de reforzar el centro del campo en el pasado mercado estival. En teoría, Flick ya contaba con muchos jugadores en la medular y de incuestionable calidad. Sin embargo, cuando se presentó la oportunidad de fichar a Rodri, no se lo pensaron en Can Barça. Por dos motivos. El primero, por su incuestionable calidad. No en vano, ha sido Balón de Oro. Pero también por su capacidad de liderazgo en el equipo, algo que el Barcelona va a necesitar si quiere llevarse la Champions, que es el gran objetivo de esta temporada. Viendo el partido que hizo Rodri en Mestalla, la cosa va bien encaminada. Era la primera vez que jugaba como titular con el Barcelona. Y se salió. Rodri tiene la gran virtud de estar en todos los sitios. Parte de la posición de pivote y reparte juego, pero no se limita a eso, ni mucho menos. En Mestalla hizo de casi todo. Fue en varias ocasiones un central más, tal vez por eso no han reforzado el centro de la zaga, ayudando a sus compañeros a desbaratar el juego ofensivo del rival. Otras veces fue mediapunta, adelantando su posición y jugando más cerca del área rival. Y ahí también destaca su faceta defensiva, como se pudo comprobar en el cuarto gol, cuando recuperó el balón en la medular. Pero incluso se le vio jugando en banda y profundizando hasta la línea de fondo para dar un pase al área, como si de un extremo se tratara. Un partido completísimo. «Todo lo que hace Rodri tiene sentido. Es emocionante. No solo en el campo, también en el vestuario. Es un auténtico líder», dijo Hansi Flick a la conclusión del partido, muy contento por su juego.
