articles.title: Cristian Tello cuelga las botas
articles.standfirst: El exjugador del Barcelona y del Betis, entre otros, pone fin a una carrera de 512 partidos profesionales tras su última experiencia en Emiratos Árabes Unidos
articles.summary: El exjugador del Barcelona y del Betis, entre otros, pone fin a una carrera de 512 partidos profesionales tras su última experiencia en Emiratos Árabes Unidos
articles.body: Cristian Tello ha decidido poner fin a su carrera profesional. El extremo catalán, de 35 años, anunció su retirada a través de un emotivo mensaje en redes sociales, cerrando una trayectoria que le llevó desde La Masia hasta algunos de los campeonatos más importantes de Europa, Estados Unidos y Oriente Medio. Tras más de una década y media en la élite, el futbolista considera que ha llegado el momento de abrir una nueva etapa lejos de los terrenos de juego. El nombre de Tello quedó ligado para siempre al FC Barcelona. Formado en la cantera azulgrana, irrumpió en el primer equipo bajo las órdenes de Pep Guardiola gracias a una velocidad endiablada y una capacidad de desborde que le convirtieron en una amenaza constante por la banda. Con la camiseta culé disputó 86 partidos oficiales, marcó 20 goles y levantó títulos como LaLiga, la Copa del Rey y la Supercopa de España. Tras su salida del Camp Nou, el atacante construyó una sólida carrera internacional. Defendió los colores del Oporto, Fiorentina y Real Betis, donde vivió algunos de los años más estables de su carrera y conquistó la Copa del Rey de 2022. Más tarde amplió su aventura futbolística en Los Angeles FC y en varios clubes de Arabia Saudí y Emiratos Árabes Unidos, convirtiéndose en uno de los futbolistas españoles con un recorrido más extenso fuera de nuestras fronteras. En su despedida, Tello agradeció el apoyo recibido por compañeros, entrenadores, aficionados y, especialmente, su familia. "El fútbol me lo ha dado todo", señaló el ya exfutbolista, que se marcha después de acumular 512 partidos como profesional.

articles.title: Elversberg's Bundesliga miracle: How tiny village team is taking German football by storm after unlikely rise up the leagues
articles.summary: Elversberg were playing regional football in the fourth tier in 2022 but have now won their first two Bundesliga matches; Adam Bate goes to see them and speaks to technical director Josef Welzmuller to find out more; "It sounds like magic or a fairytale," says Welzmuller
articles.body:
Eschewing the percentage football that they themselves noted had worked for Hamburg upon their return last season, Elversberg decided to double down. They are sticking to the principles of possession and pressing that have taken them from the fourth tier.

"We have a very clear idea of how we want to play, how we want to be on and off the field," says Josef Welzmuller, their technical director. That clarity just brought Elversberg two wins from two in this debut season. They are Bundesliga sensations already.

Bayer Leverkusen, champions of Germany just two years ago, were dispatched on the opening weekend. Now, five-time Bundesliga winners Borussia Monchengladbach have gone the same way - vanquished 4-3 in their own stadium. Curiouser and curiouser.

This victory was even more astonishing than the last. After blowing Leverkusen off the park in the first half last weekend, Elversberg did it differently this time around. They were 3-1 down after an hour and did not take the lead until the 94th minute. Gladbach stunned.

It was a privilege to be there to witness Elversberg's ambitious approach pay off. There was no thought of settling for the draw at Gladbach. Bundesliga mainstays humbled by the smallest club to ever play in the competition. None of this should be happening.

Welzmuller himself finds it all a little bemusing. If you had never heard of his team then he has sympathy as a native of Munich. "A four-hour drive away and most people there won't know about Elversberg." Picking it out on a map is not easy even for Germans.

It has been a remarkable rise. The regional leagues were the natural home of Elversberg until three promotions in five seasons took them into another orbit entirely. Their coach Vincent Wagner referred to it as their journey to Mars. Two games in and they have lift off.

Elversberg are on six points already and no team in the Bundesliga has scored more. They are two points ahead of champions Bayern Munich who they welcome next week to a stadium that needed redeveloping just to satisfy second-tier regulations in 2023.

Even now, a temporary permit is allowing Bundesliga football to be played there while further work is ongoing. All of which raises the obvious question. How exactly have they pulled it off? Putting that to Welzmuller, he insists there is no secret behind this miracle.

"I know that it sounds like magic or like a fairytale," he concedes. "But as far as I can tell, after four-and-a-half months, it is just like being very clear and being very hard working and having this very, very calm environment. A lot of hard-working people."

The reference to four-and-a-half months is an allusion to the fact that Welzmuller himself is new to this, arriving eight games before Elversberg's promotion. Ole Book, the man who masterminded much of the recruitment was poached by Borussia Dortmund in March.

Wagner was only appointed last year. His predecessor Horst Steffen was the man who had guided Elversberg out of regional football but he had a better offer from Werder Bremen, who then sacked him halfway through last season. Clearly, this is not about one man.

Wagner seemed to be making that point himself amid the jubilant scenes at Borussia-Park on Saturday. As supporters chanted his name, he pointed at his assistants who oversaw the comeback. He had been sent off at half-time. Nothing derails Elversberg.

"What I see is a structure that will hold, even if a head coach leaves, even if a sporting director or technical director leaves. In my opinion, the main factor is really how we make decisions. Very, very few people decide, so we are very fast in decision-making."

Book pulled off some particularly good deals. He loaned Nick Woltemade and Fisnik Asllani. Younes Ebnoutalib, since sold to Eintracht Frankfurt, was found at FC Giessen. But that combination of bargain buys and smart loans continues to fuel Elversberg.

Against Leverkusen, what turned out to be the winning goal was scored by David Mokwa, a young striker plucked from Hoffenheim's reserves in January. Cole Campbell, the club's record signing from Dortmund, marked the occasion with a debut goal too.

Against Gladbach, it was more of the same. Elversberg were the top scorers in their division last season, with the best disciplinary record, and their football just smells of optimism. Francis Onyeka almost scored early in the game through his pressing but hit the post.

Mokwa then ran through and did score. The lively Campbell was dispossessed for the third Gladbach goal but the substitute who replaced him, Maurice Krattenmacher, scored twice either side of Felix Keidel's glorious free-kick and Elversberg won it.

Krattenmacher's second was set up by fellow substitute Noel Futkeu. All six of the players mentioned above are aged 23 or under. Campbell and Krattenmacher are new signings. Onyeka and Futkeu are on loan from Leverkusen and Frankfurt, respectively.

Welzmuller admits being able to attract these talents is evidence that Elversberg are operating within a different world now. "Being able to buy players like Cole Campbell was far away from a club like Elversberg half a year ago," he explains.

"Being confronted by those types of situations where people recognise Elversberg and where players who were out of reach by far from us and now we are able to even acquire them, those kind of situations are where we start to realise we are in the Bundesliga."

But they are not just there, they are thriving. Perhaps the stripped-back nature of the club is the key to it. The Bundesliga is full of big clubs with attendances four times the size of the whole village of Elversberg. But many are weighed down by the expectations.

With so many stakeholders, these organisations can be like oil tankers to turn around. Agile Elversberg are different. "Compared to big clubs in Germany, where you have this kind of negative media impact and people pointing fingers, we do not have all that."

It is food for thought. And maybe when there are fewer checks and balances, things can go wrong just as quickly as they have gone right. But for now, Elversberg are the story in German football. And keeping feet on the ground is becoming more and more difficult.

"We want to be very humble, respect the league and try our best to stay up," insists Welzmuller. But they are not playing like a team with such modest aims. Next up, it is Bayern Munich. Win that and Elversberg are going beyond Mars and into another galaxy.

articles.title: Manchester United v Sabah: Meet Azerbaijani club's coach Valdas Dambrauskas
articles.summary: Lithuanian coach Valdas Dambrauskas cut his teeth in English football, and now returns in the Champions League with Sabah.
articles.body:
On Thursday, Valdas Dambrauskas will walk out at Old Trafford as manager of Sabah in the Champions League.

The Lithuanian's career will come full circle, some 20 years since he made his first steps into coaching with Manchester United Soccer Schools.

"This is beyond my imagination," Dambrauskas told BBC Sport. "To go through that tunnel on to that pitch.

"I've been many times to Old Trafford with the kids, and now I'm going to come as a coach."

This only scratches the surface of Dambrauskas' remarkable story.

It begins with an appearance on the Lithuanian version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, Dambrauskas using his modest winnings to move to London and forge a career in football.

It is a tale of casual jobs, a determination to succeed and a nomadic coaching career across Europe - which now brings the 49-year-old back to England in the Champions League with the Azerbaijani club.

How a game show gave Dambrauskas his break

As Sabah's players and staff celebrated reaching the Champions League two weeks ago, unbeknownst to Dambrauskas he was becoming a social media star.

It all related to that appearance on Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? in 2002.

Not because he was on the show, but how he spent the money he won.

"This is so long ago," said Dambrauskas with a wry smile. "A back-in-the-year story that really was forgotten.

"And now suddenly everybody is speaking about this."

Dambrauskas walked away with 4,000 litas (about £725). That might not sound like much, but it was six months' wages to the average Lithuanian.

For Dambrauskas, the real story should be his career and not a game show.

"Everybody now takes only this part, you know, about the money," Dambrauskas said. "But yes, it is a true story.

"My idea was somehow I will try to go on these [coaching] courses to gain the coaching badge, maybe go back one day to Lithuania and start to work as a football coach."

What began with Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? would map out his whole career.

'I was doing two, three, sometimes four jobs'

Dambrauskas says he had known since the age of 12 he would not make it as a player, but coaching would keep him close to football.

He arrived in London in August 2002 aged 25 on a student visa with limited English.

What followed would be eight years of hard work where he would coach for community projects, at a semi-professional club, within professional youth programmes - and hold down multiple jobs while raising two children.

In 2004 he enrolled on a course in sports science and coaching at London Metropolitan University, the first real step in his career.

Then he started out coaching by volunteering with the Access to Sports Project for deprived children in Finsbury Park.

He went on to work with London Tigers, a charitable community organisation which runs teams from junior level right through to semi-professional.

Starting out as a volunteer, across five years he progressed to manage the first team in non-league football in the Spartan South Midlands League, FA Cup and FA Vase.

Dambrauskas became the first Lithuanian to achieve a Uefa coaching licence through the London Football Association.

"I went on every possible course, every possible conference, London Football Coaches Association meetings," Dambrauskas said.

"Everywhere I could go just to gain some information, some knowledge, some extra diploma, extra course.

"That was very important for me and I took my chances."

He got his first break at a professional club when Manchester United Soccer Schools took a chance on him in 2004.

Dambrauskas spent five years coaching on residential courses in the UK and in Europe.

"That was the best thing that could happen in my life," Dambrauskas said.

"I went through three or four interviews. I will be forever grateful to [Foundation chief executive] John Shiels, the way he gave me this chance, because I didn't have experience.

"I'd never been in a place with so many great personalities as I got in the Manchester United Soccer Schools."

After a short spell with Fulham, Dambrauskas moved to Brentford. He credits academy director Ose Aibangee as one of the biggest influences on his career, pushing his limits.

All the while he was juggling home life and working multiple jobs to make ends meet.

"I was a gardener, a handyman, doing newspaper rounds at the beginning, also polishing floors in a pub," Dambrauskas said.

"So many jobs. Working in retail, and then as a sports development officer, then a sports development manager, and the central YMCA.

"I was doing two, three, sometimes four jobs."

As well as the trip to Manchester United this week, Sabah will complete their Champions League group games at Arsenal in January.

This also feels like fate for Dambrauskas - one of the buildings at London Metropolitan University on Holloway Road overlooked Emirates Stadium.

When asked about his time in England, Dambrauskas' face lights up.

"When I hear this word 'England', it for me sounds like opportunities," Dambrauskas said.

"It was really amazing. England gave me all this and I'll forever be grateful."

From England to 13 trophies in five countries

Dambrauskas was working three jobs - at Brentford, London Tigers and as a sports development manager - when the opportunity arose to coach full-time.

It meant leaving England to return to Lithuania, champions Ekranas appointing him assistant first-team and reserve-team coach at the end of 2010.

After four years at Ekranas he was named manager of Zalgiris Vilnius, Lithuania's biggest club, where his career really took off.

Dambrauskas won two league titles, three Lithuanian Cups and two Lithuanian Super Cups across three seasons - including a treble in 2016.

Then came a series of moves in which Dambrauskas took charge of eight teams over nine years in seven countries.

First RFS, with whom he won the Latvian Cup, and then Gorica in Croatia.

A third league title came with Bulgarian side Ludogorets Razgrad, along with another Super Cup and Europa League qualification.

Dambrauskas then returned to Croatia with Hajduk Split, a time which he described as "absolutely amazing" as the club won the Croatian Cup - their first trophy for 10 years.

Next up was a spell in Greece with OFI Crete, then Omonia in Cyprus - who qualified for the Conference League - and Diosgyori in Hungary.

Finally, in the summer of 2025, he arrived at Sabah, the 10th club of his career.

Dambrauskas completed the league and cup double in his first season, as the club won the title for the first time.

It took his trophy tally to 13 across five countries.

Dambrauskas had to navigate four knockout ties to get Sabah to the Champions League, and they are the only club to make it all the way through from the first qualifying round.

Welsh club TNS, Finland's KuPS, Danish side Aarhus and Israel's Hapoel Beer-Sheva were all knocked out.

The final qualifying game was as dramatic as Dambrauskas' own story.

Sabah were going out, then a goal by Tellur Mutallimov in the fourth minute of stoppage time sent the tie into extra time. They went on to win 5-2 on the night and 6-4 on aggregate.

"To go to the Champions League is something beyond imagination," Dambrauskas said.

"We have never qualified for the Conference League, we have never qualified for the Europa League. We have never passed more than two rounds in a row in one competition, and now suddenly we are here."

Sabah are based in the town of Masazir - 30 miles north of the Azerbaijan capital Baku - with a population of just 19,000.

Known as the Owls, Sabah were only formed in 2017 and on Tuesday will celebrate their ninth birthday.

Like many small clubs, their Bank Respublika Arena home, with a capacity of less than 9,000, does not meet Uefa regulations. Instead, the club are expected to play their matches at the Olympic Stadium in Baku.

Sabah will host Borussia Dortmund, Barcelona and Napoli, and face a trip to Villarreal - as well as the visits to England.

"It can be a very hard draw, and it can be a Sabah draw," said Dambrauskas, clearly excited by the prospect.

"You dream for this, to play in this competition, to play against those teams.

"So now is the time to show that you can handle it, to find a way to compete and we will try to do this.

"We have a good team, we have an ambitious team, we have hungry players who are really keen to show themselves."

Sabah president Magsud Adigozalov last week was full of praise for Dambrauskas' impact.

"His influence goes beyond tactics," Adigozalov told Report. "He has instilled a mindset and winning mentality in the team.

"Even in the most difficult moments, the team never abandons its game or fighting spirit, which is the result of the coach's work."

Twenty years ago, Dambrauskas looked out over the pitch at Old Trafford during one of his job interviews, dreaming that one day he would stand in one of the dugouts.

Now his coaching career will return to where it started.

"I lived in England when the battle between Manchester United and Arsenal was the biggest rivalry. Alex Ferguson and Arsene Wenger," Dambrauskas said.

"Now I'm going to come back as a coach in the Champions League and hear that anthem. It's really amazing."

articles.title: Troy Parrott stuns old boss Jose Mourinho as Kylian Mbappe costs Real Madrid, plus lots more in the Euro Debrief
articles.summary: Barcelona seize the initiative in LaLiga as Troy Parrott comes back to haunt Jose Mourinho; Adam Bate picks out the big stories from the continent in the Euro Debrief, a Sky Sports column focusing on the major European leagues and more...
articles.body:
Welcome to The Euro Debrief , a new Sky Sports column in which Adam Bate rounds up some of the key stories from the latest matches across the continent. This week:

Goalscoring goalkeeper in the Eredivisie

LaLiga: Barca win big, Jose sick as a Parrott

It was a big weekend for Barcelona as they capitalised on Real Madrid's slip up at Real Betis to move clear at the top of LaLiga. The five-goal thrashing of Valencia featured some standout performers with Pedri applauded off by the home fans at Mestalla.

But Lamine Yamal was sensational, getting two goals and creating more chances than anyone else on the pitch. Fermin Lopez also scored one, assisted by Anthony Gordon, and set up two. Valencia, who brought on Harvey Elliott for his debut, had no answer.

Jose Mourinho's Madrid are going to have to be very good indeed to keep pace with this Barcelona and cannot afford too many evenings like the one they had in Sevilla. Kylian Mbappe's poor penalty in stoppage time meant they returned to the capital pointless.

Madrid were wasteful throughout, squandering five big chances in the first half alone and were punished by Troy Parrott. The Irishman fired in on the rebound on his home debut, having once been given his Premier League debut for Tottenham by Mourinho of all people.

How can you not be thrilled for Parrott? The sight of him wide-eyed and emotional taking in the joy of the Betis fans at the final whistle at La Cartuja was a reminder of the journey he has been on. One recalls speaking to him when he first went to AZ Alkmaar.

"It is just about experiencing new things," he told Sky Sports in that interview. "There are not many people that do it. So, to try something new, it is exciting for me. It is a short life that we have. And I am not even just talking football now." His amazing adventure continues.

As for Mourinho, he had enjoyed a drama-free start until now but there were signs of familiar mischief-making as he accused Betis, led by his old foe Manuel Pelllegrini, of cynicism in buying fouls and complained about his own side's naivety. A hint at what is to come?

The pick of the other games in Spain was probably at Villarreal where Deportivo A Coruna continued their encouraging return to the top division by winning 3-2. Adama Traore was even able to get away with a quite extraordinary headed own goal on debut.

It mattered not as Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, reborn at Deportivo, scored the winner in the 88th minute. The 37-year-old former Arsenal and Barcelona forward has netted in each of his first four appearances for the Galician club. They remain unbeaten.

LaLiga results: Real Sociedad 0-0 Celta Vigo, Real Betis 1-0 Real Madrid, Athletic Club 3-0 Atletico Madrid, Rayo Vallecano 3-2 Racing Santander, Villarreal 2-3 Deportivo A Coruna, Valencia 0-5 Barcelona, Alaves 5-2 Osasuna, Malaga 0-0 Levante, Espanyol 1-1 Sevilla.

Bundesliga: Schalke somehow stifle Bayern

It was an absolute thrill to be at Borussia-Park to witness Elversberg's first-ever Bundesliga away win as they came from two down to win 4-3 against Borussia Monchengladbach. The opening-weekend victory over Bayer Leverkusen was no fluke.

This was more dramatic. Elversberg were two adrift for longer than they led. But they impressed throughout with their enterprising football and this village club, who were playing regional football four years ago, are becoming one of the stories of the season.

If you would like to read more about that, the full story of how they are shocking the Bundesliga is covered here , but in this Euro Debrief it is perhaps sufficient to state that Elversberg - Elversberg - are two points ahead of Bayern Munich in the table.

That is because Bayern were somehow shut out for the first time in over a year by a stubborn Schalke side that held them to a goalless draw in Gelsenkirchen. Vincent Kompany did rotate but the big names came on and were unable to force a winner either.

Most notably, Harry Kane was denied brilliantly by Loris Karius in what was a remarkable rearguard action. Schalke had only 17 per cent of the possession but, having visited the club to interview their charismatic coach Miron Muslic, that is hardly a surprise.

"We have no possession because we do not want possession," he told Sky Sports in that conversation earlier this year. Schalke were third bottom for possession in winning the second tier, let alone facing Bayern. "We define our game completely differently."

Elsewhere in Germany, Stuttgart, who took the opposite approach against Bayern the previous week and were punished for it, bounced back with a big win, while there was also three more points for Borussia Dortmund in more dramatic fashion at Hoffenheim.

BVB were two down after an hour but Serhou Guirassy's deft finish and even better assist for Fabio Silva to score in his third game in a row levelled it up. Ethan Nwaneri then crossed for Albian Hajdari's late own goal. A fine debut for the Arsenal loanee.

On Sunday, there was the opportunity to attend another thriller as Augsburg went top of the table. Being at Eintracht Frankfurt to see that one was special as the perennial overachievers came from behind to score four second-half goals for a sensational win.

Bundesliga results: Stuttgart 4-1 Cologne, Bayer Leverkusen 4-0 Union Berlin, Borussia Monchengladbach 3-4 Elversberg, Hoffenheim 2-3 Borussia Dortmund, Paderborn 0-1 Freiburg, Werder Bremen 3-1 RB Leipzig, Schalke 0-0 Bayern Munich, Hamburg 0-5 Mainz, Eintracht Frankfurt 1-4 Augsburg.

Serie A: Inter make comeback, Amorim denied

Massimiliano Allegri knows San Siro better than most having had two spells in charge of AC Milan but this was a first. The experienced coach, now at Napoli, had never lost a game there from 2-0 up. But that is what happened on Saturday as Inter showed their resolve.

When Rasmus Hojlund doubled the advantage for Napoli in the second half, things looked bleak for the champions but Lautaro Martinez scored his second of the game to win it 3-2 in stoppage time. The Argentina international really is a genuine Inter great.

These goals move him to third outright on the all-time list of Inter top scorers in Serie A. Above him are Giuseppe Meazza, after whom the stadium is named, and Benito Lorenzi who left Inter in 1958. For Martinez to have outscored all the greats since is some feat.

Gian Piero Gasperini would have been horrified if Roma had not been able to muster their own comeback against his former club Atalanta in the Stadio Olimpico. His current team came from behind to win 2-1 in the 93rd minute with the very last of their 39 shots.

That is the most by any team in any game in Europe's major leagues so far this season. Eighteen of them came in the first half, but Ederson scored with Atalanta's second soon after the break. Roma were rewarded with two late goals to make it three wins from three.

Elsewhere, Como picked up another fine win as they put four past Genoa. But it was the end of the road for Fabio Grosso. He was sacked by Fiorentina after Che Adams' late goal for Torino left them bottom of the Serie A table with three defeats out of three.

In Sunday's action, Jay Robinson scored for Monza. The English teenager is on loan from Southampton. But most eyes were on the late game between Juventus and AC Milan in Turin. The home side salvaged a point in stoppage time but neither truly convinced.

Ruben Amorim has Milan organised, although their opener from Alphadjo Cisse midway through the second half was their only shot on target in the match. Juve deserved their leveller through fellow substitute Federico Gatti and both retain their unbeaten records.

Serie A results: Genoa 1-4 Como, Fiorentina 1-2 Torino, Inter 3-2 Napoli, Roma 2-1 Atalanta, Frosinone 3-2 Venezia, Parma 1-1 Monza, Bologna 2-2 Sassuolo, Juventus 1-1 AC Milan.

Ligue 1: Problems for PSG after Monaco loss

Monaco's finances might be under scrutiny after their deadline-day dramas but there are no issues on the pitch as they beat Paris Saint-Germain 2-1 at the Parc des Princes to make it three wins from three and extend their lead over winless PSG to seven points.

Stanis Idumbo fired in the winner from an acute angle as Monaco turned things around in the second half. It was fiercely struck but Matvey Safonov's failure to keep it out has sparked debate over his position in France with calls for Lucas Chevalier to return.

There is still a suspicion that PSG were fortunate to retain their European crown without a top-class goalkeeper. Could it cost them this time around? This slow start is certainly food for thought for Luis Enrique, who should have been celebrating his new contract.

Maybe he anticipated it? "It does not matter if you are Champions League winners two years in a row, you have to keep changing because the rivals adapt to what we do." PSG have had chances in their first three games, but Luis Enrique is seeking new solutions.

Elsewhere in Ligue 1, on-loan Southampton striker Cameron Archer scored on his debut for Auxerre but could not stop Lyon running out 3-1 winners. Paulo Fonseca's men are still smarting from their Champions League play-off exit but now sit third in the table.

Strasbourg put six past Troyes and are now the league's top scorers, Rennes won at Angers, while Liam Rosenior continued his excellent start with Paris FC with a 3-2 win over Marseille at the Velodrome. Lassine Sinayoko scored all three for Rosenior's side.

Ligue 1 results: Toulouse 0-1 Lille, Lyon 3-1 Auxerre, PSG 1-2 Monaco, Lens 0-1 Lorient, Le Havre 1-2 Brest, Nice 1-1 Le Mans, Troyes 2-6 Strasbourg, Angers 1-2 Rennes, Marseille 2-2 Paris FC.

Elsewhere: Koeman's 'keeper son scores two

It was De Topper in the Netherlands as Ajax hosted PSV and it was the away side that won 3-1 to once again assert their dominance over their old rivals. Tolu Arokodare notched again for Ajax but the champions for the past three seasons were too strong.

Jordi Cruyff has overseen major changes at Ajax this summer in his role as technical director with 11 incomings and 17 players going out. Overall, a significant profit has been made but, as he did at Barcelona, Cruyff has targeted experienced acquisitions.

Marc-Andre ter Stegen, Thilo Kehrer, Daley Blind and Sofyan Amrabat are among the new signings at Ajax in the belief that their presence will bring more stability and allow the young talent to shine. This setback suggests it is still a long journey back to the top.

The best story in the Netherlands came at Telstar where the son of a former Ajax and PSV player did the unthinkable. Ronald Koeman Jr scored two penalties to help Telstar come from two down to draw. Impressive enough but Koeman is a goalkeeper.

And yet, in this week of all weeks, the only way to finish is with a couple of comeback victories. Over in Portugal, the reigning champions Porto came from behind to maintain their perfect record with a 2-1 win over Moreirense at the Estadio do Dragao.

And in the big game in Turkey, Fenerbahce lost 2-1 at home to Besiktas. Dusan Vlahovic followed up his hat-trick on Monday by completing the comeback to leave Fenerbahce four points behind Galatasaray, who snatched a late winner at Basaksehir on Friday.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Rangers' Lawrence Shankland blow, Celtic lose Hyun-Jun Yang, is pressure on at Hibs, Aberdeen & Kilmarnock?
articles.summary: Rangers beat Motherwell 1-0; Celtic won 2-1 at St Mirren; Hibs lost 2-1 at St Johnstone; Hearts beat Dundee 2-1; Aberdeen vs Kilmarnock was goalless; Dundee United drew 1-1 with Falkirk; watch St Johnstone vs Celtic on Wednesday night, live on Sky Sports from 7.30pm
articles.body:
We may be less than two months into the new Scottish Premiership season, but there is already plenty of drama and talking points.

While Rangers and Celtic will have to cope without key players for very different reasons, some managers are already feeling the heat after a struggling start.

Martin O'Neill's Hoops remain the only team on maximum points and are already 16 points ahead of the league's current bottom side, Kilmarnock.

Lawrence Shankland could be facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines just as he was finding his feet at Rangers.

The striker appeared to suffer a hamstring injury in Saturday's win against Motherwell - an issue which kept him out at Hearts for three months last season.

Ryan Naderi did come on to score the only goal against the Steelmen and Rangers did bring in £9m striker Kevin Kelsy on deadline day, so you could argue it is not an area they are short in.

But, Shankland's injury comes after they had already lost forward Youssef Chermiti for a "significant period" with an ACL injury.

There is also Bojan Miovski, but he has struggled to get a consistent run since his move to Ibrox from Girona last summer.

He scored 13 in all competitions in his first season at Ibrox, averaging a goal every 142 minutes. Naderi's average for Rangers last season was a goal every 203 minutes.

Compare that to Shankland's average under McInnes at Hearts last season - that was a goal every 86.5 minutes.

Hyun -Jun Yang scored the winner for Celtic at St Mirren and is becoming an instrumental player as they made it five victories from five in the Premiership this season.

But, they will now have to cope without him for their next four games as he heads off to the Asian Cup with South Korea.

From a player who almost left the club in January, to excelling under Martin O'Neill's guidance.

Two goals and an assist in seven games show his influence this season.

Last term, he scored 10 goals and provided three assists.

Yang is impressive on the flanks and would likely be the first choice on the left were it not for his international commitments.

Hearts ended last season in second, and that is where they currently sit after their dramatic last win at Dundee.

After losing McInnes, Shankland and Cammy Devlin to Rangers in the summer, many questioned how much success they would have under new head coach Wouter Vrancken.

But after some bruising European defeats and a loss to Aberdeen on the opening day of the Premiership, they are unbeaten and deserve to be at the top end of the table.

While Hearts are impressing, it is a very different situation across the capital at Hibernian.

After losing the Edinburgh derby in midweek. a loss to Premiership newcomers St Johnstone appears to have ramped up the pressure on David Gray.

The head coach is always just a few poor results from fan criticism, next they face a trip to face League One side Ross County in the League Cup. A game now fraught with danger for the former Hibees captain.

Aberdeen were booed off after their goalless draw with Kilmarnock, leaving Stephen Robinson with just one Premiership win in five.

The expectations are high at Pittodrie, but they have scored just three league goals while conceding six and the fans are furious.

Robinson brought in 14 new players this summer, but it is clear he is yet to find his best XI. How much time does he have to turn things around?

If things are bad for Gray and Robinson, then spare a thought for Killie boss Neil McCann.

Saturday's point against the Dons is the best his side have managed after he saved them from relegation at the end of last season.

It is four goals scored vs 14 against for the Rugby Park side in the Premiership as McCann admits they have let the fans down. But the former Dundee boss insists he and his players can turn things around.

After a point at Pittodrie, they take on Aberdeen again this weekend in the League Cup quarter finals. A must-win match for both managers.

articles.title: Harry Souttar: Leicester City players 'take responsibility' for Oxford defeat
articles.summary: Leicester players failed to produce the "bare minimum" and "have got to take responsibility" for Saturday's heavy defeat by Oxford, says captain Harry Souttar.
articles.body:
Leicester City players failed to produce the "bare minimum" and "have got to take responsibility" for Saturday's heavy League One defeat by Oxford United, says captain Harry Souttar.

The 4-0 home loss ranks as the club's worst league result in history, having never been beaten by such a margin when so far down the divisions.

It raised doubts about the future of head coach Russell Martin, with the fan backlash instant and bitter, while former Foxes forward Matt Piper described it as a "sackable performance" during his post-match analysis on BBC Radio Leicester.

While Martin's approach to the game - his rigid instance on playing the possession heavy football which been branded as "passing teams to death" - has been heavily criticised, defender Souttar says the players will take the blame for Leicester's latest capitulation.

"It doesn't matter what kind of football you want to play - if you don't compete in the game, if you don't win duels, you don't win tackles, you don't win headers, then you're not going to give yourself a chance in the game," he told BBC Radio Leicester.

"I felt in the first half we played some OK stuff but we didn't compete, and obviously it got brought up at half-time, and again in the second half that cutting edge wasn't there, and that's solely down to the players.

"I think that's the bare minimum and we fell below that. We've got to take responsibility for that."

'That's a sackable performance' - what next for Martin at Leicester?

Oxford Utd thump Leicester to heap pressure on Martin

Foxes pain and Burnley suffer hangover - Aaron McLean's EFL takeaways

Pre-match, post-match and topical Foxes content

Australia international Souttar has remained with the Foxes after back-to-back relegations despite intense interest in him from Championship clubs Sheffield United and Wrexham after he featured at the summer's World Cup.

He has stepped up as skipper in the new-look, youthful Foxes side under Martin, having been called upon just five times by Leicester in the past three seasons.

Souttar's only two appearances for Leicester last season came after they were already relegated, having spent the preceding 16 months recovering from a knee injury that he suffered while on loan at Sheffield United a season earlier.

And before that, he was barely called upon in the 2023-24 season by then Leicester manager Enzo Maresca who, like Martin now, placed a heavy emphasis on passing out of defence as part of the possession-obsessed approach that the club has committed to for a number of years.

Against Oxford, Souttar started in defence in front of veteran goalkeeper Alex McCarthy and alongside the experienced Luke Thomas, but the backline also included two novices in 20-year-old Jayden Joseph and Manchester City teenage loanee Christian McFarlane.

The pair were two of five starting players that were under the age of 22 and who have been turned to by the Foxes hierarchy to get them out of the third tier at the first time of asking after a long list of high profile and highly paid players – including ex-England midfielder Harry Winks, Denmark defender Jannik Vestergaard and Ghana forward Jordan Ayew - were moved on in the summer.

Souttar said the Foxes were "frustrated" by their shortcomings against Oxford, just days after Leicester earned their first league win of the season against Plymouth Argyle.

"In the Plymouth game midweek we looked really good and we felt we could kick on again. It didn't happen," Souttar said.

"We'll be men about it, I know that it was far from good enough. And we'll look back at the game, look at the moments that we've simply got to do better.

"All we can do as a playing group is put it right next weekend."

Leicester are in next in action on Saturday against Stockport County, who are third in the table and coming off a 4-0 win against Wigan Athletic.

articles.title: Los reajustes de Uriarte se cruzan con las bases del Plan AC Aurrera
articles.standfirst: Socios consideran que determinadas actuaciones sobre la gobernanza que afectan a la representación del club deberían de ser llevadas a la Asamblea de Compromisarios
articles.summary: Socios consideran que determinadas actuaciones sobre la gobernanza que afectan a la representación del club deberían de ser llevadas a la Asamblea de Compromisarios
articles.body: La buena marcha adquirida por el equipo de Terzic, que este sábado jugará para enlazar la tercera victoria consecutiva y constatar la ilusión generada en el inicio de Liga tras levantarse con éxito y buen juego de dos derrotas choca con la realidad insitucional. El club ha implementado una serie de medidas que señalan a la institución y la comprometen ante sus socios. Las acciones que ha tomado Uriarte deberían pasar el tamiz de la próxima Asamblea General de Socios Compromisarios atendiendo a las bases del Plan AC Aurrera. En concreto, queda más que sustanciado en dos de sus argumentos fundacionales: mantener nuestra filosofía, identidad, valores y estilo Athletic Club. Mantener el control sobre las decisiones del Club por parte del socio. Después de retirar entradas de cortesía a veteranos -la Agrupación de Veteranos se repartía alrededor de una centena-; empleados del club y proponer una rebaja del cupo por partido que correspondían a los responsables federativos; ofrecer a los expresidentes un asiento vitalicio en el palco tras retirarles las invitaciones de que disponían en Tribuna Sur Alta, el club ahora ha dado un paso adelante y ha trasladado al resto de equipos de la Liga, según ha desvelado este lunes El Correo, que no dará invitaciones para ningún partido y que sólo atenderá a los representantes del club que acudan al palco. Las medidas ceñidas a los ajustes en las entradas afectan al estilo de club y cordialidad social de la entidad. Y esa puerta es un elemento irrenunciable para consultar y lograr la aprobación del socio. De momento, los expresidentes ya se han pronunciado al respecto alertando de que se pone en riesgo la institucionalidad del club. Por cierto, ninguno de ellos quiso acudir al asiento de nuevo cuño reservado en el palco….y no hay idea de hacerlo. La crisis de las entradas suspende las localidades de intercambio que recoge la Liga como “aquellas que los clubes destinan a patrocinadores, familiares de jugadores y compromisos institucionales del club visitante”. La decisión del Athletic tendrá un efecto recíproco. Se da por hecho que mantener esa idea exigirá al club rojiblanco de una limitación máxima de su representación en los desplazamientos para no tener que hacer frente al pago de unas localidades que antes eran invitaciones. El asunto no se ha cerrado todavía porque la intención del presidente es que los futbolistas del primer equipo también tenga limitado el acceso a invitaciones, aunque les reservarían un cupo de entradas de pago. El club advirtió al grupo de que no dispondrían de entradas ya desde el partido ante el Atlético, pero la protesta de la plantilla, que incluyó en la misma otros problemas internos de la entidad que hacen referencia a jugadoras del femenino, trabajadores de Lezama y a distintos colectivos de las categorías inferiores, levantó el pie de la decisión. Será así al menos hasta que se produzca una reunión entre dirigente y capitanes. Dicho encuentro lleva ya 10 días buscando fecha.

articles.title: Premier League: Why is Sunderland vs Arsenal at 8pm on Saturday?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why Saturday's Premier League fixture between Sunderland and Arsenal is kicking off at 8pm
articles.body:
Defending Premier League champions Arsenal head to Sunderland on Saturday evening, with their match at the Stadium of Light kicking off at 20:00 BST.

The unusual kick-off time has been used on a few occasions by the league in recent seasons.

Because Arsenal are playing away at Napoli on Wednesday night in their first Champions League fixture of the season, the late kick-off allows them extra recovery time to prepare for the trip to Sunderland after returning from Italy.

Typically, clubs selected to play in the Saturday lunchtime fixture that are also playing a Champions League fixture on the previous Wednesday get the option of kicking off at 12:30 or 20:00 on that Saturday.

Arsenal were not given that choice because the match had already been rescheduled before the Champions League fixtures had been announced, with the Premier League having anticipated the possibility of the Gunners playing in Europe before their trip to Sunderland .

It was also moved to a later kick-off in the interest of avoiding any late rescheduling for supporters that are attending.

Some clubs who are given the choice of kick-off times by the Premier League may opt for the 12:30 Saturday slot instead of 20:00 if they are playing again the following midweek, to increase recovery time before that fixture.

Arsenal will play three matches at 20:00 BST in the space of six days. The trip to Sunderland comes in between hosting Napoli in the Champions League and a trip to Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup.

As this fixture is this weekend's designated live game on TNT Sport, it means there will be no match at 12:30 on Saturday. The later kick-off on Wearside effectively acts as a replacement for the lunchtime game.

Typically, the Premier League's primary fixture slots are 20:00 on Friday, 12:30, 15:00 and 17:30 on Saturday, 14:00 and 16:30 on Sunday and 20:00 on Monday.

articles.title: Las estrellas de la Champions se despiden: adidas presenta su último balón
articles.standfirst: Nike releva a la marca alemana desde 2027
articles.summary: Nike releva a la marca alemana desde 2027
articles.body: Adidas presentó, como cada año desde hace más de dos décadas, los balones oficiales de la Champions League y la Women's Champions League para la temporada 2026-27. El masculino recupera la estética de niebla que evoca los entrenamientos a puerta cerrada, con un acabado metalizado que atraviesa las estrellas del torneo y los logos en rosa intenso. El femenino se inspira en el concepto 'Ring of Light': once estrellas, una por cada jugadora sobre el césped, en tonos morados combinados con dorado y naranja sobre un fondo blanco con detalles plateados. Hasta aquí, una presentación rutinaria. Pero esta vez el lanzamiento tiene fecha de caducidad. Es el último balón de estrellas que fabricará adidas para la máxima competición europea. Después de 25 años, la marca alemana pone fin a una era. adidas viste el balón de la Champions desde 2001, cuando lanzó el primer 'Finale' con el diseño de estrellas que remite al trofeo de la competición. Desde entonces, cada edición ha mantenido esa identidad visual como sello distintivo, hasta convertirla en una de las imágenes más reconocibles del fútbol europeo. La propia compañía es dueña en exclusiva de los derechos sobre ese patrón de estrellas, lo que condiciona directamente lo que viene después: quien la releve no podrá heredar el diseño, tendrá que inventar otro desde cero. Ese relevo lo protagonizará Nike. Según informó en su día el Financial Times, citando a una persona conocedora de las negociaciones, la marca estadounidense pagará a la UEFA algo más de 40 millones de euros al año por convertirse en la nueva proveedora del balón, prácticamente el doble de lo que abonaba adidas. El nuevo contrato, que arrancará en la temporada 2027-28 y se prolongará hasta 2031, no se limita a la Champions: por primera vez, un único proveedor vestirá también la Europa League y la Conference League. El último balón con estrellas rodará en la final de 2027, el 5 de junio en el Metropolitano de Madrid. A partir de ahí, Nike tendrá que presentar un diseño propio junto a la UEFA, sin poder recurrir al patrón que adidas ha protegido durante 25 años. El movimiento encaja en una estrategia más amplia de la marca del swoosh. Nike ya perdió este año el contrato del balón de la Premier League, que recayó en Puma. Hacerse con el balón de la Champions, la Europa League y la Conference League de golpe es la manera más directa de recuperar terreno visible frente a adidas en la competición de clubes más seguida del continente. adidas se despide con un balance que resume bien lo que deja atrás: 25 años y, según sus propias palabras, "la gama de balones más icónica de todos los tiempos".

articles.title: Los ultras del MAS Fez 'reivindican' Ceuta y Melilla con un polémico tifo
articles.standfirst: Un sector de la grada del conjunto marroquí exhibió un pancarta en español reivindicando la soberanía de Marruecos sobre las dos ciudades autónomas en la Champions africana
articles.summary: Un sector de la grada del conjunto marroquí exhibió un pancarta en español reivindicando la soberanía de Marruecos sobre las dos ciudades autónomas en la Champions africana
articles.body: l fútbol africano vivió este fin de semana un episodio que trascendió por completo lo deportivo. Los aficionados del Maghreb Association Sportive de Fez (MAS Fez, el campeón de Marruecos), desplegaron una enorme pancarta en las gradas del Complexe Sportif de Fez con el mensaje "Ceuta y Melilla: dos ciudades, una patria: Marruecos", aprovechando el estreno de su equipo en la Liga de Campeones de la CAF frente al Rahimo FC de Burkina Faso. La acción se produjo en uno de los fondos del estadio y fue protagonizada por seguidores vinculados al grupo ultra Fatal Tigers, uno de los colectivos más numerosos de la afición del club marroquí. El tifo, redactado íntegramente en español, permaneció visible durante los primeros minutos del encuentro y fue acompañado por cánticos y un importante despliegue de banderas en la grada. El episodio llega, además, en un momento especialmente sensible para las relaciones futbolísticas entre ambos países, con España, Portugal y Marruecos ya inmersos en la organización conjunta del Mundial 2030, un proyecto que exige una colaboración estrecha entre las tres federaciones justo cuando este tipo de gestos vuelven a poner sobre la mesa las diferencias territoriales de fondo. Mientras tanto, sobre el césped, el campeón marroquí cumplió con nota. El MAS Fez se impuso con claridad por 4-1 al Rahimo FC en la ida de la primera ronda previa de la máxima competición continental africana. Sin embargo, el abultado triunfo quedó eclipsado por una pancarta que volvió a evidenciar cómo el fútbol puede convertirse en escaparate de reivindicaciones políticas y territoriales más allá de los 90 minutos.

articles.title: Las Palmas juega contra el reloj de las ausencias
articles.standfirst: De la Barrera verbalizó su preocupación tras el empate ante el Leganés
articles.summary: De la Barrera verbalizó su preocupación tras el empate ante el Leganés
articles.body: Las Palmas juega estos días obligada a competir mientras espera que el parte médico deje de crecer. El empate sin goles ante el Leganés volvió a poner delante del espejo una realidad que Rubén de la Barrera no quiso esconder: "Tenemos a muchísima gente importante fuera que no están disponibles". Son siete las ausencias físicas -más la sanción de Jesé- que arrastraba el equipo. Cinco de ellas -Ale García, Cedeño, Viti, Recoba y Opoku- todavía sin haber podido estrenarse: "Las ausencias influyen, no es disculpa, es realidad", sentenció el técnico. Una realidad que obliga a Las Palmas a caminar por un alambre. Y en ese alambre han aparecido los más jóvenes. La cantera ha dejado de ser una promesa para convertirse en una necesidad: "Los pibes que van entrando nos van ayudando muchísimo", reconoció el técnico. Ahí están Rafa Cruz, con solo 16 años, Pezzolesi, Elías o Iñaki, futbolistas a los que el contexto ha empujado al primer plano. Pero el problema no termina en los que están fuera. Clemente se perdió los dos primeros partidos por lesión. Iñaki lleva "dos años sin jugar 90 minutos", como apuntó el técnico. Caro apenas tuvo presencia el curso pasado. Bonfanti e Iván Jaime tuvieron que asumir peso casi desde que cruzaron la puerta de entrada y Sandro, después de un último año prácticamente en blanco, "lo quiero hacer sentir de nuevo importante". Demasiadas sillas vacías para un vestuario que, al mismo tiempo, tiene que salir cada semana a pelear por los tres puntos. Recuperar el equilibrio mientras compite es el mayor desafío de esta Las Palmas. De la Barrera no buscó excusas después del Leganés, solamente describió el paisaje: "Mientras todo eso sucede, uno tiene que ir ganando puntos". Porque las lesiones pueden detener a un futbolista, pero no detienen a la competición.

articles.title: Belgian FA still wants Folarin Balogun ban answers
articles.summary: Belgium's FA says it still wants answers about why Folarin Balogun was allowed to play against them at the World Cup.
articles.body:
Belgium's Football Association says it still wants answers about why Folarin Balogun was allowed to play against their team at the World Cup - and have asked for the issue to be on the agenda at the next Fifa Council.

In one of the most controversial moments of the summer's World Cup, Balogun was cleared to play for co-hosts USA in the last-16 tie with Belgium after a one-game ban following a straight red card in his previous game was suspended for a year by Fifa.

That was a highly unorthodox decision and received widespread criticism, especially after it emerged US President Donald Trump and White House officials had lobbied Fifa.

European governing body Uefa and the Royal Belgian Football Association (RBFA) were among those to question the decision.

The RBFA said it had asked Fifa for "a clear justification of the decisions taken and details on how such situations will be handled in the future".

Balogun - who scored three goals up to that stage - started in the game, which Belgium won 4-1. The Red Devils lost to Spain in the quarter-finals.

In a statement on Monday, the RBFA said it now wants the issue discussed on the Fifa Council meeting on 15 October - and says it will not support Gianni Infantino's bid for a further term as Fifa president.

RBFA president Pascale van Damme said: "Two months after the events, our questions remain unanswered.

"Given the importance of transparency and clarity for all parties involved, we request the necessary explanations and, at the same time, wish to explore where improvements to the current processes are possible, so that similar cases can be handled in a clear, consistent and efficient manner in the future.

"Together with Uefa, the other confederations and the national associations, we remain committed to transparency in decision-making, strong governance and clear processes. We remain open to constructive cooperation, in the interest of the trust, integrity and future of football."

Balogun's red card was the 189th in World Cup history and only the second, after Brazil's Garrincha in 1962, to not serve a suspension.

Fifa never fully explained the decision, just citing "article 27 of the Fifa disciplinary code" which allows it "to fully or partially suspend the implementation of a disciplinary measure".

No other suspensions were lifted at the 2026 World Cup.

Infantino, who has been Fifa president since 2016, confirmed this week he will stand for re-election in March.

The Swiss has been under huge pressure after details of a now-abandoned plan emerged that sought to sell stakes in Fifa competitions, including the World Cup, to private investment firms.

Belgium's football governing body is the latest to join the growing list of those to say they do not want Infantino to remain in the role.

The RBFA added its two reasons for refusing to support Infantino were the Balogun case and the Fifa Forward Enterprise to sell those stakes.

articles.title: La lista de España para el Mundial: Valverde y Pascual desvelan sus ochos
articles.standfirst: Así lo hicieron este lunes en Sevilla
articles.summary: Así lo hicieron este lunes en Sevilla
articles.body: sAlejandro Valverde ya tiene prácticamente cerrada la selección española que disputará el próximo Mundial de carretera en Canadá, apenas una semana después de que termine LaVuelta. Salvo contratiempo de última hora, el seleccionador cuenta con ocho nombres fijos para afrontar una carrera que considera especialmente atractiva para las características del bloque español. Así lo contó este lunes en Sevilla. Juan Ayuso, Carlos Verona, Enric Mas, Raúl García Pierna, Iván Romeo, Marcel Camprubí, Igor Arrieta y Markel Beloki son los ocho corredores elegidos por Valverde para representar a España. Una mezcla de experiencia, escaladores y jóvenes con capacidad para adaptarse a una prueba que se presenta mucho menos controlable que otros campeonatos recientes. El propio Valverde explicó sus sensaciones sobre una cita en la que ve opciones para varios corredores. “Es un Mundial muy abierto, donde se abre todo mucho más”, señaló el seleccionador, satisfecho además con un trazado que encaja con las características de la selección: “Es un recorrido que nos viene muy bien”. Ayuso aparece como una de las principales bazas españolas, pero no será necesariamente una selección construida alrededor de un único líder. La presencia de Enric Mas, actualmente inmerso en la pelea por LaVuelta, permite disponer de otra carta importante para los momentos más duros. A su lado estarán corredores de enorme capacidad para trabajar y anticiparse como Verona o García Pierna, además del talento de una nueva generación encabezada por Romeo, Camprubí, Arrieta y Beloki. Berrade, que estaba en la plrelista, estará en el Europeo. La proximidad entre LaVuelta y el Mundial será uno de los factores que habrá que gestionar. Apenas habrá una semana entre el final de la ronda española y la prueba mundialista en Canadá, por lo que el estado físico con el que terminen corredores como Mas o García Pierna será determinante. En cualquier caso, la idea de Valverde está clara y, si no aparece ningún problema físico, estos serán los ocho hombres que estarán en el Mundial. En categoría femenina, la selección española también contará con algunas de sus principales referencias. Mavi García, Paula Blasi, Sara Martín, Usoa Ostolaza, Mireia Benito y Sandra Alonso forman parte del bloque previsto para competir en Canadá. Benito y Blasi harán la crono. España llegará así al Mundial con una selección masculina especialmente profunda y con diferentes alternativas para una carrera que Valverde espera abierta. Sin una superioridad tan marcada de un único corredor y en un circuito que considera adecuado para los españoles, el seleccionador quiere aprovechar todas las opciones que pueda ofrecer la carrera.

articles.title: Neco Williams handball: New video shows ball hitting arms
articles.summary: A new camera angle shows the ball coming off Nottingham Forest defender Neco Williams' arms as he scores his disallowed goal against Tottenham.
articles.body:
New video footage has been released that shows the ball coming off Neco Williams' arm in the lead-up to his disallowed goal in the 0-0 draw against Tottenham Hotspur .

The Nottingham Forest defender bundled the ball home in the 67th minute but video assistant referee Peter Bankes stepped in to rule out the goal for accidental handball.

Williams and Forest manager Oliver Glasner were adamant after the match that there was no proof the ball touched an arm.

While the footage vindicates the VAR's decision, it may not end the arguments about the decision to rule out the goal.

'At not one moment did I think I handballed it'

It has been a tough couple of days for Bankes, because while the VAR was 100% confident he had made the correct decision, it has attracted intense media scrutiny.

He will now feel vindicated - but there is one important distinction to make.

The new camera angle was not one of those available to Bankes during the game - so it is unlikely to end the anger from Forest fans over the validity of the intervention, even if we know the VAR was ultimately correct.

On the new footage, Williams touches the ball with his left arm then his right forearm before it goes into the net.

The VAR hub only has access to the broadcast cameras, and this camera was one of several which does not transmit as part of match coverage.

Bankes believed the proof on the angles he had available came from the ripple of Williams' shirt as the ball touched his right forearm.

Former midfielder Danny Murphy said on Match of the Day he could understand the argument for the handball but was not convinced the goal should have been ruled out.

"It's a really tricky one," Murphy said. "Maybe it could be a tiny bit on his sleeve or right forearm. But is it clear and obvious? No. That's the answer."

BBC Sport understands that Pro Ref - the new name for the refereeing body that was previously called Professional Game Match Officials (PGMO) - is completely happy with the decision to rule out the goal.

There is irritation within Pro Ref about how the story has developed, partly because Williams was so unequivocal that the ball had not touched his arm - when there is now evidence to the contrary.

"I've seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it," Williams told Sky Sports.

"I have seen all the images and at not one moment can you tell that has clearly hit my arms, because it never. I knew straight away I've headed it down in between my arms. It didn't hit my arm."

The feeling is that if Williams had not been so certain with his comments that the criticism would not have been as strong.

The new evidence also shows the ball did not touch his head, although because it all happened in a split second it is conceivable he was not aware of that.

Nottingham Forest have been approached for comment.

Much of the commentary on the incident has centred around the VAR not having evidence of a clear and obvious error as a reason to disallow the goal.

Glasner mentioned it and Williams posted on X to that effect too.

But clear and obvious errors only cover subjective incidents - those that require the referee to go to the pitchside monitor to review an incident.

Factual interventions, such as handball before a goal, are evidence-based judgements made by the VAR.

If the VAR feels they have the proof of an offence, they will disallow the goal.

For all Forest's disquiet, there are plenty of people who believe you can see the handball, and Bankes was clearly one of those.

It shows one of the issues with VAR that can never be solved - even the factual interventions like this are, in truth, subjective. It is one person's judgement that others can disagree with.

A case in point is Benjamin Sesko's goal for Manchester United against Liverpool last season.

The ball looked as if it might have brushed the fingertips of the Slovenia striker before going into the goal, but the VAR Stuart Attwell felt he could not be certain and allowed the goal to stand.

Referees' chief Howard Webb later said the ball "probably does hit the hand" but "the VARs need to see that conclusively".

Attwell did not feel he had proof, but Bankes did.

During pre-season media briefings, Webb said attacking handball was one law he would change - which would mean goals like Williams' would not be ruled out based upon the original evidence.

"The problem is the law forces VARs on every goal to look at what body part the ball went in off," Webb said.

"If you were only to penalise when the attacker deliberately handles the ball or makes himself unjustifiably big - and not have that forensic examination - you could 'check complete' it more quickly.

"It is a law I would definitely look to change. So Pro Ref and the Premier League are going to try and lobby for that to be changed."

VAR is being operated with a lighter touch this season. So far there have been just two subjective interventions at 0.06 per game, compared to 0.15 last season.

However the generally negative narrative around VAR and the tribal nature of football mean its involvement in key incidents attracts widespread attention.

articles.title: Eric García sufre fractura nasal y jugará con máscara contra el Levante
articles.standfirst: El catalán ya se ejercitó hoy con protección
articles.summary: El catalán ya se ejercitó hoy con protección
articles.body: Eric García acudió esta mañana a la Ciudad Deportiva y se ejercitó sin problemas pese a la fractura nasal que sufrió ayer domingo en Mestalla. El catalán se entrenó, no obstante, con una máscara, que deberá lucir en los próximos compromisos. No es la primera vez que el polivalente futbolista debe jugar con protección. Eric García tuvo que ser sustituido antes de la media hora del encuentro contra el Valencia. El internacional, que ayer jugó de lateral derecho, recibió un golpe en la nariz tras una acción fortuita con su compañero Rodri. Las pruebas a las que se sometió confirmaron que sufre una fractura nasal. El azulgrana se ejercitó, sin problemas, esta mañana en la Ciudad Deportiva y lució una máscara. Eric es baja por sanción contra el Feyenoord, en el cruce de este miércoles de la Champions League, pero podrá jugar sin problemas contra el Levante el próximo domingo. Eso sí, lo hará con una protección. No será, de todas formas, la primera vez que el internacional juegue con máscara. El curso pasado, sin ir más lejos, también padeció una fractura del tabique nasal que le forzó a saltar al terreno de juego con una careta durante varias semanas. Fue en el mes de noviembre, en el campo del Brujas en el partido de la fase de la liguilla de la Champions League: en la disputa de un balón aéreo chocó con la cabeza de Vermant. El futbolista se adaptó pronto y bien al antifaz.

articles.title: Mourinho: "¿El penalti en La Cartuja? Quiero pensar que el VAR no sabía el reglamento"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador luso atendió a los medios en la rueda de prensa previa al debut en Champions ante el Inter
articles.summary: El entrenador luso atendió a los medios en la rueda de prensa previa al debut en Champions ante el Inter
articles.body: El Real Madrid afronta su debut en Champions League tras sufrir el primer tropiezo de la temporada. Lo hará ante el Inter y en el Santiago Bernabéu en el camino hacia la soñada Decimosexta. En la previa, José Mourinho atendió a los medios en una rueda de prensa en la que reflexionó sobre la no repetición del penalti en La Cartuja y no dio pistas sobre quién ocupará el medio. Partido de mañana: "Quiero ganar. Te puedo decir que quiero jugar bien, pero no quiero jugar bien como jugamos contra el Betis y perder. Estamos en una fase donde jugamos ocho partidos y el objetivo es clasificarnos. Quiero pensar este partido como único". Estado del vestuario: "Los he visto como me gusta verlos. Muertos en el vestuario en Sevilla y ya recuperados en el entrenamiento del domingo. Hoy perfectamente, normales. Hemos tenido la convicción de haber hecho buen partido. Los goles que hemos fallado es una anormalidad. Tenemos problemas conocidos, pero ya está. Vamos a jugar y competir". ¿Qué le ayuda más, la frustración con la Champions o los buenos recuerdos?: "He perdido una semifinal por penaltis, pero no pienso en eso. Ni positivo ni negativo. Pienso que soy entrenador del Real Madrid y que mañana se juega un partido de Champions que no es ultra importante. Creo que ambos nos clasificaremos, y es una posibilidad estar ambos en el futuro. Cada punto es importante. El Inter también viene en busca de sus puntos". La malicia que le falta al equipo: "Es cuestión cultural. Quizá se percibe de modo negativo, pero no es una crítica. Mañana lo entenderás fácil". Trent en el mediocampo: "No te lo voy a comentar. Perdona. Podría hablar y dar muchas vueltas. No estarán los tres (Bernardo, Camavinga y Güler). El algoritmo ha decidido. La pregunta es obvia, yo la esperaba. Pero ahí estamos. Tenemos cinco opciones y podemos hablar de todas, pero al final no voy a decir nada". Champions en el pasado: "Con el Madrid son dos períodos distintos. Cerré en 2013, con lo que ganamos y lo que perdimos. Es un capítulo cerrado. Son momentos diferentes. En 2010 no se llegaba a cuartos de final desde hace años, semifinales tampoco. Ahora en los últimos diez años han ganado seis Champions. Obviamente tengo ilusión por ganar la Champions con el Madrid, pero separado del contexto". ¿Qué club se ha encontrado a la vuelta?: "Encontré a un club que es el Real Madrid. Real Madrid es Real Madrid. Es suficiente decir eso. Tuvo una complicada temporada. Tienes cosas que mejorar en ese caso, con la estabilidad y con la base más problemática. Queremos ganar cada partido y cada competición. Tenemos que ir hacia este nivel de estabilidad". ¿Qué veremos mañana en sus jugadores?: "No quiero hablar de criterio arbitral. Voy a escapar de tu pregunta, perdona. Perdimos con el Betis, porque no traducimos en goles la producción ofensiva que el equipo ha tenido. Pero el penalti... ¿por qué no ha sido repetido? ¿Es porque el VAR no conoce el reglamento o porque no ha querido? Si el VAR no lo ha repetido por desconocimiento, tiene que ir a casa y no hacer el VAR. Si es porque no ha querido, todavía peor. Si no sabían el reglamento, ¿por qué no llamaron al árbitro para verlo en el monitor? Es extraño. Yo quiero ir en la dirección de la honestidad y pensar que no sabía el reglamento. Quiero dejar claro que no hemos perdido por eso, porque quizá hubiésemos fallado el penalti, pero me gustaría saber por qué no ha sido repetido. La otra cosa es por qué el capitán Vinicius se lleva una tarjeta amarilla. Va al árbitro y le muestra amarilla. El capitán tiene el derecho de ir al árbitro para pedir una explicación". Endrick: "Mañana puede estar preparado para jugar 5 minutos, 10 máximo. Entrenó ayer por primer vez con el primer equipo y no juega desde Budapest. No tiene condiciones para más, pero tenemos espacios abiertos del banquillo y ahí está. Jugará en ataque, tranquilo que no jugará de lateral izquierdo o central. Por derecha o izquierda, 9 o 10". ¿Qué siente al enfrentarse a Chivu? Habló con él: "Ha sido mi jugador, hemos trabajado juntos. Pasamos por tantas cosas juntos, las buenas y las malas. ¿Con quién has hablado tú para saber si tengo mala relación con él? ¿Con quién?".

articles.title: Ratko Mladic: Red Star fans display tifo of war criminal
articles.summary: Red Star Belgrade fans unveil a tifo of war criminal Ratko Mladic before their derby win over Partizan Belgrade on Sunday.
articles.body:
Red Star Belgrade fans unveiled a tifo of war criminal Ratko Mladic before their derby win over Partizan Belgrade on Sunday night.

Mladic, who died in a United Nations prison in August, was given a life sentence for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity in 2017.

He and his troops were responsible for the systematic killing of the non-Serb population of Bosnia-Herzegovina during the wars in the former Yugoslavia between 1992 and 1995.

He oversaw the massacre of 8,000 men and boys at Srebrenica and a siege of the capital Sarajevo in which more than 10,000 people died.

Red Star have already been fined 90,000 euros (£77,000) this season by Uefa , external after their fans unveiled a banner commemorating Mladic in a Europa League play-off against Czech side FC Viktoria Plzen last month.

Red Star's social media accounts published a video of the tifo and the two teams observing a minute's silence for Mladic, alongside a saluting emoji.

The official X account of Bosnia-Herzegovina's national team replied with an obscenity.

After initially enjoying the protection of Serb president Slobodan Milosevic, who would later die while on trial for genocide himself, Mladic spent more than a decade on the run, eventually being found hiding out in a remote farmhouse.

However, he remains a celebrated figure for some in Serbia with thousands gathering at a church in Belgrade for his funeral on Monday. , external

articles.title: El momento en que Hernández Hernández amonestó a Vinicius y que indigna a Mourinho: "Es el capitán"
articles.standfirst: Las cámaras de Movistar Plus captaron el instante en el que el colegiado mostró la cartulina al brasileño en el Villamarín
articles.summary: Las cámaras de Movistar Plus captaron el instante en el que el colegiado mostró la cartulina al brasileño en el Villamarín
articles.body: El Real Madrid se fue de vació en el Benito Villamarín el pasado viernes con la derrota por la mínima ante el Betis por 1-0... y también con varios cabreos en la mochila. Uno de ellos, el penalti que acabó deteniendo Álvaro Valles a Mbappé y que, a juicio de Mourinho, como ha reconocido hoy en la rueda de prensa previa al duelo ante el Inter, debería haberse repetido. El otro tema de enfado fue la cartulina amarilla que vio Vinicius con el partido ya acabado. Hoy, las cámaras de Movistar Plus han captado el momento en el que el 7 brasileño, con el brazalete de capitán, se acercó al colegiado para hablar sobre algo una vez había señalado el final del encuentro. Tras una conversación acalorada, el colegiado grancanario le muestra la tarjeta amarilla, a pesar de que Vinicius le sigue insistiendo que lleva el brazalete y que, como capitán, puede dialogar con el árbitro. Hoy, sobre esto, Mourinho también se ha quejado ante los medios de comunicación. "Por qué el capitán del Real Madrid, Vinícius, se lleva una tarjeta amarilla? Se dirige al árbitro y antes de llegar ya le saca tarjeta amarilla. ¿Por qué motivo? Siempre nos dicen que el capitán puede pedir explicaciones al árbitro...", ha indicado el portugués. "El futbolista Vinicius Junior fue amonestado por el siguiente motivo: realizar observaciones de carácter técnico a una de mis decisiones una vez finalizado el encuentro, encontrándonos aún sobre el terreno de juego", puso Alejandro Hernández Hernández en el acta.

articles.title: Hyundai se convierte en Socio Oficial de la Champions League hasta la temporada 2030-31
articles.standfirst: El fabricante coreano ha llegado un acuerdo con la máxima competición de clubes en Europa que entra en vigor en la temporada 2026/27 y se prologará durante cinco años.
articles.summary: El fabricante coreano ha llegado un acuerdo con la máxima competición de clubes en Europa que comienza en la temporada 2026/27 y llegará hasta 2031.
articles.body: Hyundai se ha convertido en nuevo socio automovilístico oficial de la Champions League, en virtud de un acuerdo que arranca en esta temporada 2026/27 y se prolongará hasta el final de la 2030/31. La marca coreana ha valorado en gran medida que la Champions League sea la competición de clubes más vista del planeta cada año, con casi una de cada tres personas en el mundo interesada en su seguimiento, según los datos que maneja la propia organización. De hecho, el formato actual de la competición reúne a 36 equipos de las principales ligas europeas, lo que multiplica el atractivo comercial del torneo para extender la imagen de la firma oriental. Para Hyundai, el desembarco en la Champions League llega tras casi tres décadas ligada al fútbol de máximo nivel (empezaron en 1999), con presencia histórica en grandes torneos internacionales y en clubes de distintos continentes (el Atlético de Madrid, entre ellos). La marca coreana ha tenido además presencia en el Mundial de este verano, un antecedente reciente que la propia compañía sitúa como paso previo natural hacia su llegada a la máxima competición europea de clubes. José Muñoz, presidente y consejero delegado de Hyundai Motor Company, ha afirmado respecto a este acuerdo que el fútbol "une a las personas como casi nada más lo hace, más allá de idiomas, fronteras y generaciones". Por su parte, Xavier Martinet, presidente y director ejecutivo de Hyundai Motor Europe, ha señalado que "tanto la Champions League como Hyundai se mueven por el progreso, el rendimiento y la ambición de unir a las personas". El primer modelo vinculado de forma directa a este acuerdo será el IONIQ 3, un compacto eléctrico que Hyundai comenzó a fabricar este verano en su planta de İzmit, en Turquía, y que forma parte de los cinco lanzamientos que la marca prevé para el mercado europeo a lo largo de la temporada 2026/27. Aunque Hyundai es coreana, hay que recordar que mantiene presencia en Europa desde hace más de tres décadas, con su centro técnico y su centro de diseño ubicados en Rüsselsheim (Alemania) y plantas de producción en República Checa y Turquía. Además, la marca distribuye sus vehículos en los mercados europeos a través de una red de más de 2.000 puntos de venta y posventa que forman la estructura sobre la que se apoya ahora su llegada como socio oficial de la Champions League.
